en: {The Procedure for Daily Duties} Now, [the Procedure for Bathing].
Homage to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
"O Lord of the Forest, grant us longevity, strength, fame, luster, progeny, sustenance, and wealth; grant us the sacred word, wisdom, and retentive memory.
This is the mantra for cleaning the teeth.
"Salutation to the Infinite One, who possesses a thousand forms, a thousand feet, eyes, heads, thighs, and arms;
salutation to the eternal Puruṣa, who has a thousand names and sustains thousands of millions of yugas.
Thus [performs] the washing of the left foot.
"Salutations to the one whose navel is a lotus; salutations to you who recline upon the waters;
salutations to you, O Keśava, Ananta, Vāsudeva; let there be salutations to you. Thus is the washing of the right foot.
"May the Gaṅgā, Prayāga, Gayā, Naimiṣa, Puṣkara, and whatever other holy fords (tīrthas) exist on earth, [attain their merit] through the grace of Hari."
May they come into my cupped hands, which are like lotuses, and wash away the stain upon the moon of my face.
"One should bathe at a sacred ford; among equals, one becomes a sacred ford.
The malice of the stingy man is to be deprecated; O Brahmaṇaspati, protect us from the mortal who seeks to harm.
Thus [performs] the rinsing of the mouth.

Oṃ, obeisance to Gāyatrī. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our intellects (3). Thus ends the [section on] the sacrificial thread (*yajñasūtra*). Having tied the head-knot with the Gāyatrī itself:
"The supreme, most pure sacrificial thread (*yajñopavīta*), which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning..."
Put on this foremost, auspicious life-prolonging sacred thread; may there be strength and splendor for you.

"Thou art the sacred thread; I bind thee on with the upper garment of the sacrifice. Having thus performed the wearing of the sacrificial thread (*yajñasūtra*), one should perform the washing of the feet, then drink pure water three times, and wipe the mouth twice. Then, with the thumb and forefinger, one should touch the two nostrils while they contain water.
One should touch the pair of eyes with the thumb and ring finger, the pair of ears with the little finger and thumb,
the region of the navel with the palm, and then the heart, head, and shoulders with the fingers.
Then follows the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma). Oṃ, [the deities] beginning with Agni belong to Brahmā. Homage to Agni who dwells in the waters;
homage to Indra; homage to Varuṇa; homage to Vāruṇī; homage to the Lord of Waters; homage to the Waters. Thus is the salutation.
At the final bath (avabhṛtha), the Triṣṭubh meter and Varuṇa are [the presiding deities].

"King Varuṇa has indeed made wide for the sun a path to follow; he has provided feet to set down where there was no place, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart. Thus is the worship of King Yama, in the Jagatī meter, addressed to Varuṇa.
"O Varuṇa, those hundred and those thousand great sacrificial nooses that are spread out—
may the god Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, all the gods, and the Maruts, who possess beautiful voices, release us from them. Thus one should repeat this over water three times.

"May the waters of Nicāṅkuṇa and Śunaḥśepa be friendly to us; may the waters and the plants be auspicious. May they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate. With these words, one should cast three handfuls of water toward the left side.

"O Varuṇa, whatever offense we humans commit against the divine folk, whether through thoughtlessness or even in accordance with your law, O God, do not cause us harm because of that sin. Having thus paid homage, one should then divide the clay into three portions and pour water upon the first portion, saying: "Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ" (three times).

In the second part, there is the sprinkling of water. [The hymn] of Trita is "The Great Lineage of the Ādityas": "O Ādityas, for you are renowned as those who extend from the shore of the quarters to the very heavens; you are like good bathing-places accessible from every side.
Your aids are easy to attain, even when we are driven away; your aids are indeed excellent, your aids are indeed excellent."
In the third part, there is the sprinkling of water; the meter is Gāyatrī, the sage is Medhātithi, and the deity is Viṣṇu.
"Therefore may the gods protect us from where Viṣṇu strode forth with the seven abodes of the earth.
Then, having divided one-third into four parts, he should cast them into the four directions.

"Indra is the great [lord] of Bharga; since we fear, O Indra, from that [fear], grant us freedom from fear. O Maghavan, be gracious; with your protections, slay our enemies and those who oppose us. Thus [it is said] in the former [portion].

"May Indra, the subduer of enemies, the lord of the people, the slayer of Vṛtra, the self-controlled one who bestows well-being, go before us—Indra, the bull, the drinker of Soma, the granter of fearlessness. Thus [he says] over the southern [post]:
"O you free from demons, drive away the subduers; break apart the jaws of Vṛtra!"
"O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, free from anger against the enemy who seeks to harm," thus [ends] the western [verse].
This is a *triṣṭubh* by Vasukra, addressed to Indra: "Understand this well for me, O singer:
the rivers carry the curse back; the hyenas [attack] the lion, the fish [attack] the one facing them, and the jackal [attacks] the boar."
From the eighth enclosure;
thus, in the subsequent [enclosure], the Anuṣṭubh is the earth of the sacrifice.
O Earth, trodden by horses, trodden by chariots, and trodden by Viṣṇu;
you were lifted up by the boar-form Kṛṣṇa with his hundred arms.
O Earth, I take you along with progeny and wealth;
O Earth, you are bestowed by Brahmā and consecrated by Kaśyapa.
O Earth, take away my sin, whatever evil deed has been committed by me—
whether done by speech, performed through action, or even conceived in the mind.
O Earth, grant me nourishment; everything is established in you.
By the removal of my sin through you, may I go to the world of Brahmā.
Thus, with the second clay mixed with water and consecrated by the mantra, one should purify the area from the navel upwards.
Then, having divided the first portion into four parts, Rudra [is assigned] to Kutsa and the Jagatī meter.
"Do not harm us in our bodies, nor in our offspring, nor in our life; do not injure us in our cattle or our horses.
O Rudra, do not slay our heroes in your wrath; bearing oblations, we shall worship you with reverence.
Having thus smeared the forehead and the other parts [of the body] with clay.

Having smeared [the body] with the second portion—saying "Oṃ bhūḥ, Oṃ bhuvaḥ, Oṃ svaḥ" on the left shoulder; "Oṃ mahaḥ, Oṃ janaḥ, Oṃ tapaḥ" on the right shoulder; and "Oṃ satyam" on the heart—one should then perform a prostration.
I shall now describe the invocation of the sacred fords (tīrtha), which I will explain immediately hereafter:
Kurukṣetra, Gayā, Gaṅgā, Prabhāsa, and the Puṣkara lakes.
May all these sacred fords be present for me at the time of bathing;
I take refuge in the god Varuṇa, the powerful lord of the waters.
"Grant me the sacred ford that I have requested for the removal of all sins;
I take refuge in all the Rudras, the givers of boons, and I am one who dwells within the waters."
Bowing down and standing firm, I take refuge in all those who dwell in the waters;
I take refuge in the god Agni, who dwells in the waters and is the destroyer of sins.
I likewise seek refuge in the waters, which are meritorious and purifying;
and in Rudra, Agni, the serpents, Varuṇa, and the waters themselves.
"May they quickly pacify my sin and may they always purify me"—
having spoken thus, one should then perform the ritual cleansing (saṃmārjana) in the water.
Then, having taken a handful of water together with a third part of the clay;
We know the Lord of Waters; we meditate upon the one who holds the noose in his hand; may that Varuṇa inspire us. (3) Om Tat Sat.

O Brahman, today, on this lunar day of such-and-such a month and such-and-such a fortnight, on this specific tithi, for the purpose of removing the sins acquired through my own body, speech, and mind— [The remainder of the text follows: ...I shall perform the ritual bath with the sacred thread on, according to the rules, for the sake of longevity, health, strength, fame, prosperity, happiness, and the attainment of all desires, as well as for the removal of all obstacles. May the gods, the sages, the ancestors, the protectors of the quarters, the guardians of the world, the lords of the world, the lords of the waters, the serpents, the yakṣas, the rākṣasas, the piśācas, the bhūtas, the pretas, the kṛtyās, the vināyakas, the grahas, the planets, the nakṣatras, the rivers, the mountains, the forests, the earth, the sky, the wind, the fire, the sun, the moon, the stars, the Vedas, the Purāṇas, the Itihāsas, the Dharmaśāstras, the Smṛtis, the Āgamas, the Tantras, the mantras, the yantras, the mudrās, the mūrtis, the liṅgas, the sthānas, the tīrthas, the rivers, the lakes, the ponds, the wells, the tanks, the springs, the oceans, the rivers, the streams, the waterfalls, the holy places, the temples, the images, the deities, the gurus, the preceptors, the disciples, the brothers, the sisters, the friends, the relatives, the kinsmen, the neighbors, the guests, the servants, the animals, the birds, the insects, the moths, the ants, the flies, the gnats, the mosquitoes, and all other living beings be pleased. May they forgive me for whatever offense I have committed against them through ignorance, negligence, or lack of awareness, whether intentionally or unintentionally, in body, speech, or mind. May they grant me their grace. May there be peace, peace, peace. Om Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ. Om. Tat Sat.]

"For the sake of pleasing Śrī Nārāyaṇa, I shall perform my bath in the current of such-and-such river; Oṃ, do so! Having thus cast [the water] into the current, he should sprinkle water upon his head with his joined palms.
Om. The wise ever behold that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, like an eye stretched across the sky.
The inspired poets, ever-watchful and full of praise, kindle that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
With "Oṃ bhūḥ, Oṃ bhuvaḥ, Oṃ svaḥ, Oṃ mahaḥ, Oṃ janaḥ, Oṃ tapaḥ, Oṃ satyam," one should purify the head.

*Oṃ haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasad dhotā vedisad atithir duroṇasat | nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtam ||* Thus is the *upasthāna* (homage). *Oṃ namo devebhyaḥ*—with the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*kaṇṭhopavītī*)—*svāhā ṛṣibhyaḥ*. With the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*apasavyena*), *svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ*.

With the left hand, [one should offer water] so that the entire universe, from Brahma down to a blade of grass—the world with its moving and non-moving beings—may be satisfied, may be satisfied, may be satisfied; may it be so.

"O auspicious one, O Vaiṣṇavī, by the touch of your head, take away that sin which has entered my skin and bones, as well as that which was committed in other births. Thus, with the remaining clay, a *tilaka* should be made.
Now follows the wearing of the garment.
The youth, well-attired and enveloped in light, has come; he becomes more excellent as he is born.
The wise poets, seeking the divine with their minds, lead him upward.

"May those born in my family who are childless and deprived of their lineage drink the water squeezed from my garment, which has been offered by me. Thus is the wringing of the bathing cloth. [Thus ends the ritual for bathing.]
[Now, the Twilight Devotions.]
Salutations to the illustrious Mahāgāyatrī. Salutations to Sāvitrī. Salutations to Sarasvatī.
Oṃ: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi) of the Praṇava, and its meter (chandas) is indeed the Gāyatrī;
Agni is the deity, and its application (viniyoga) is proclaimed to be in the vyāhṛtis.
The vyāhṛtis of Prajāpati, the ancient Parameṣṭhin, are both separate and combined; they are the syllable Om, which is Brahman.
Prajāpati is the deity of the *vyāhṛtis* taken collectively;
when they are taken individually, their deities are Agni, Vāyu, and Sūrya.
The meter for the *vyāhṛtis* is *chandas*; for those with one syllable it is called *ṛk*, and for those with two syllables it is called *atyṛk*.
Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the meter is *gāyatrī*, and the deity is Savitṛ.
In the practice of recitation (*japya*) for the invocation of the deity, the application of the *gāyatrī* is taught:
"I invoke Gāyatrī, the destroyer of all sins."
There is no mantra to be chanted superior to the Gāyatrī; there is no offering equal to the Vyāhṛtis.
Come, O Goddess, granter of boons; be present before me during my recitation.
"Because you protect one who is singing (gāyantam), you are therefore remembered as Gāyatrī.
Thus, having recollected the seer, the meter, the deity, and the application.

Having tied a tuft of hair with the Gāyatrī mantra and having sprinkled water all around himself with the Gāyatrī itself, he should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma). Thus, having offered salutation and then having joined his palms in añjali.
Having invoked the Gāyatrī with "Thou art vigor," [he recites] the seer-verse of the gods.
You are vigor, you are endurance, you are strength, you are splendor; you are the abode of the gods by name.
You are the universe, you are universal life; you are everything, you are all-encompassing life, the all-conquering one. Now, the mantra for breath control (prāṇāyāma):
Reciting: *Oṃ bhūḥ, oṃ bhuvaḥ, oṃ svaḥ, oṃ mahaḥ, oṃ janaḥ, oṃ tapaḥ, oṃ satyam;
oṃ tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi, dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt;
oṃ āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtaṃ brahma bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ.* Thus one should recite.

One should perform *prāṇāyāma* while meditating on Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva— red, blue, and white respectively— at the navel, heart, and forehead during the stages of inhalation (*pūraka*), retention (*kumbhaka*), and exhalation (*recaka*).
[One should recite] the *Gāyatrī* together with the *Vyāhṛtis*, the *Praṇava*, and the *Śiras*.
One who recites [the mantra] three times while restraining the breath—this is called prāṇāyāma.
The inhalation (pūraka) consists of one rotation; the retention (kumbhaka) is likewise double that;
and the exhalation (recaka) is said to be triple, according to the sequence of entry, stay, and exit.
Oṃ! May Agni, and Manyu, and the lords of wrath protect me from the evils committed through wrath—
whatever evil I have done by day with my mind, speech, hands, feet, belly, or genitals.

"May that which is not grasped by the hand take away whatever evil is in me; I offer this into the waters, the source of immortality, into Truth, the Light—svāhā! Thus, one performs the three evening rinsings (ācamana).
Oṃ, may Sūrya and Manyu and the lords of wrath [protect me] from the sins committed through wrath.
May they protect me!
Whatever evil I have committed during the night by thought, by speech, by my two hands, by my feet, by my belly, or by my organ;

May the Night take away whatever evil has been committed by me; I offer this into the waters, the source of immortality, into the Sun, the light—*svāhā*. Thus, three times in the morning one should sip water (*ācamana*).
*Oṃ, may the Waters purify the Earth; may the purified Earth purify me.*
May Brahmanaspati purify; may the purified Veda purify me.

"Whatever is leftover, whatever is unfit to be eaten, or whatever evil deed I have committed—may the waters purify all that in me; I offer up the acceptance of gifts from the wicked, svāhā. Thus, at midday, [one recites] the triad.
Oṃ. You, O Waters, are indeed the source of happiness; grant us strength for great joy and for the sake of vision. 1.
Of that most auspicious sap which you possess, grant us a share, as longing mothers [grant nourishment] to their children. || 2 ||
Therefore, let us come quickly to you, O Waters, for whose abode you quicken us; do you give birth to us. 3.

Oṃ! Golden-hued, pure, and purifying are those waters, in which Kaśyapa was born and in which Indra was born; those who, assuming various forms, have held Agni as their embryo—may those waters be auspicious and gracious to us. 4.
Oṃ! Those whom the gods make their food in heaven, those who exist manifoldly in the intermediate space—those [waters]... 5.
Oṃ! Those rivers in whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men—those [rivers]... 6.
Oṃ! Behold me with a gracious eye; touch my skin with a gracious body.
May those waters, which drip with sweetness, which are pure and purifying, be auspicious, pleasant, and beneficial to us. 7.
Oṃ! May the divine waters be auspicious for our desires; may they be for our drinking, and may they flow toward us for our well-being and happiness. || 8 ||

Oṃ! May the waters of the desert be auspicious to us; may the waters of the marshes be auspicious to us; may the waters of the ocean be auspicious to us; may the waters of the wells be auspicious to us. 9.
Oṃ! May the waters, our mothers, purify us; may those who cleanse with ghee purify me with ghee.
For the goddesses carry away every impurity; having bathed in them, I emerge pure and cleansed. 10.
Oṃ! O waters, carry away whatever evil is in me—whether it be malice that I have committed, or what I have left unsaid, or even falsehood. (11)
Oṃ! May they release me from the curse, and also from that which pertains to Varuṇa;
and also from the fetters of Yama, and from every sin against the gods. 12.
Oṃ! Whatever sin I have committed while awake or while asleep, may [the Lord] release me from all that transgression. 13.
Oṃ, I have performed the lustration with the curd of the victorious, spirited horse;
may it make our mouths fragrant and may it prolong our lives. (14) Thus are the mantras for sprinkling.
Oṃ, as one released from a pillar, or as one bathed and freed from impurity after sweating, [may I be cleansed].
"May the waters purify me from mental sin, as clarified butter is purified by a strainer. With these words, one should cast three handfuls of water into the left [hand].
Then: "Oṃ! From the heat of austerity, Ṛta and Satya were born."
From that, night was born; from that, the ocean and the sea arose.
From the ocean, the sea, the year was born;
he, the controller, distributed days and nights at the opening of every eye of the universe.
"The Creator fashioned the sun and moon as before, as well as heaven, earth, the intermediate space, and the sky. Reciting this while holding both hands in the midst of water, one should murmur:
"Oṃ bhūḥ, Oṃ bhuvaḥ, Oṃ svaḥ, Oṃ mahaḥ, Oṃ janaḥ, Oṃ tapaḥ, Oṃ satyam," and thus purify the head.
Oṃ, you move within all beings, dwelling in the secret cave of the heart, facing every direction;

you are the sacrifice, you are the Vaṣaṭ-call, you are the waters, light, essence, immortality, Brahman, Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svar, Om—thus [recited] three times for the ritual sipping of water (ācamana). Then follows breath control (prāṇāyāma); then, facing the sun, Oṃ.
Having recited "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ" (3),
he should cast up three handfuls of water consecrated with the Gāyatrī mantra.
Having circumambulated [the sun] clockwise with arms raised, he should worship [the sun] at dawn and dusk with the hymn beginning "Udyantam" (Rig Veda 1.50.1).
Oṃ! Rising above the darkness, beholding the higher light, we have gone to the Sun, the god among gods, the supreme light. 1.
Oṃ. His rays bear up the god Sūrya, the Jātavedas, so that everyone may behold him. 2.
Oṃ. The brilliant array of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-region; he is the soul of all that moves and stands still. 3.
Oṃ! That eye, beneficial to the gods, has risen bright in the east.
May we see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns. 4.

Oṃ. Haṃsa, dwelling in purity; Vasu, dwelling in the atmosphere; Hotṛ, dwelling at the altar; Guest, dwelling in the house; Dweller among men, dweller in the best, dweller in truth, dweller in the sky; born of the waters, born of the cows, born of truth, born of the mountains—He is Truth. 5.
Oṃ! May the radiant, vast [Soma] drink the Soma-mead; may he bestow unimpaired life upon the lord of the sacrifice.
Impelled by the wind, he protects himself; he nourishes all creatures and shines forth manifoldly. 6.
Thus concludes the midday attendance. Now, meditating upon Viṣṇu, one should recite the Puruṣasūkta.
Oṃ. Of this hymn (sūkta) in the Anuṣṭubh meter ending with a Triṣṭubh verse, the deity is the Universal Soul Puruṣa himself, and Nārāyaṇa is remembered as the seer (ṛṣi). || 1 ||
Oṃ. The Puruṣasūkta is the seer of the Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa.
Oṃ. The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.
Having pervaded the earth on all sides, he transcended it by ten fingers' breadth. (1)
The Person alone is all this—that which has been and that which is to be; he is the lord of immortality, as well as of that which grows by means of food. 2.
Such is His greatness, yet the Puruṣa is even greater than this;
all beings constitute one quarter of Him, while His three quarters are the immortal in heaven.
The Puruṣa rose up three-quarters above; one quarter of him came into being here again.
From there he pervaded the universe, reaching both the animate and the inanimate.
From him Virāj was born; from Virāj was born Puruṣa.
Once born, he extended beyond the earth—both behind and before.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with the Puruṣa as the oblation,
spring was its clarified butter, summer its fuel, and autumn its offering.
They sprinkled that sacrifice upon the sacred grass—the Puruṣa who was born in the beginning;
with him, the gods, the Sādhyas, and the Ṛṣis performed the sacrifice.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the speckled butter was gathered;
from it, he created those animals—those belonging to Vāyu, both wild and domestic.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the Rig-verses and the Saman-chants were born;
from it the meters were born, and from it the Yajus-formula was produced.
From that the horses were born, and whatever animals have two rows of teeth;
from that the cows were born, and from that goats and sheep were produced. || 10 ||
When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they arrange him?
What was his mouth, what were his two arms, and what are said to be his thighs and feet? (11)
The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; the Rājanya (Kṣatriya) was made from his arms;
that which was his thighs became the Vaiśya; and from his feet the Śūdra was born. 12.
The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born;
from his mouth Indra and Agni were born; and from his breath Vāyu was born. || 13 ||
From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved;
from his feet the earth, and from his ears the quarters; thus they fashioned the worlds. (14)
Seven were its enclosing sticks, and thrice seven were the fuel-sticks prepared;
when the gods were performing the sacrifice, they bound Puruṣa as the victim.
With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the Sacrifice; those were the first established laws.
These mighty ones attained the heights of heaven, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. 16.
Then, having formed the *saṃhāramudrā* and meditating upon Śiva, one should recite the *Śivasūkta*.
Oṃ! That divine [power] which rises far away from the waking state, that very same [power] comes forth likewise for one who sleeps;
it is the far-reaching, the sole light among lights—may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve. (1)
That by which the wise and skillful perform their rites at the sacrifice during the assemblies—that ancient, wondrous power within all creatures—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent. 2.
That which is wisdom, as well as consciousness and fortitude; that which is the inner light, the immortal among living beings;
without which no action whatsoever is performed—may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve. (3)
May that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve—by which this entire world, past, present, and future, is encompassed by the Immortal, and by which the sacrifice with its seven priests is extended. 4.
In whom the Ṛg-verses, the Sāman-chants, and the Yajus-formulas are established, as spokes are fixed in the nave of a chariot wheel;
in whom the entire consciousness of living beings is woven—may that mind of mine be of auspicious intent. || 5 ||

Like a skilled charioteer who guides horses with reins, or like a driver who leads spirited stallions, may that mind of mine—which is established in the heart, undecaying, and most youthful—be possessed of auspicious intentions. 6.
Now, that person who is in this orb, and that golden person—this very person who is in this orb is indeed this person in the right eye. || 7 ||
Now follows the Upasthiti,
the Śukriya, and that of Rudra.
He who has risen from the great ocean, shining brightly in the midst of the lake—may that bull, the red-eyed Sūrya, the wise one, purify me with his mind.
May that which we have uttered as a sacred prayer not harm us; homage, homage to the radiant Sūrya!

*Ā* at the navel; *U* at the heart; *Ma* at the head. *Bhūḥ* at the feet; *Bhuvaḥ* at the heart; *Svaḥ* at the head. *Oṃ Bhūḥ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; *Bhuvaḥ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*; *Svaḥ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*; *Mahaḥ* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*; *Janaḥ*...
Salutation to the two little fingers; salutation to austerity and truth for the palms and backs of the hands.

*Bhūḥ* at the feet; *bhuvaḥ* at the knees; *svaḥ* at the private parts; *mahaḥ* at the navel; *janaḥ* at the heart; *tapaḥ* at the throat; *satyam* at the head. *Oṃ bhūḥ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *bhuvaḥ* to the head, *svāhā*; *svaḥ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*) at the throat; *satyam* to the head. *Oṃ bhūḥ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *bhuvaḥ* to the head...
Svāhā! Svaḥ to the crest-lock, Vaṣaṭ! Mahaḥ to the armor, Huṃ! Janaḥ to the two eyes, Vauṣaṭ! Tapaḥ Satyam to the weapon, Phaṭ! *Tat savituḥ* to the two thumbs, Namaḥ!
*Vareṇyam* to the two index fingers, Namaḥ! *Bhargo devasya* to the two middle fingers, Namaḥ!
May we meditate [upon it]—salutation to the two ring fingers; may [the Lord] inspire our intellects—salutation to the two little fingers.

*Pracodayāt*: salutation with the palms and the backs of the hands. *Tat-savituḥ*: on the two feet. *Jānu*: on the two knees. *Vareṇyam*: on the waist. *Bhargaḥ*: on the navel. *Devasya*: on the heart. *Dhīmahi*: on the throat. *Dhiyaḥ*: on the nose. *Yaḥ*: on the eyes. *Naḥ*: on the forehead. *Pracodayāt*: on the head. *Tat-savituḥ*: to the heart.

*Namaḥ*. To the most excellent, *svāhā* to the head. To the splendor of the divine, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*). We meditate, *huṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*). May he impel our thoughts, *vauṣaṭ* to the two eyes. May he inspire us, *phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*). *Oṃ*: Water in the two shoulders; light in the two eyes; essence in the mouth; nectar in the forehead; *brahma-bhūr-bhuvaḥ*.
The vowels on the head.
Now, the mudrās.

Salutation to that which is equal (*tatsamāya*). Salutation to the Enclosed (*saṃpuṭāya*). Salutation to the Extended (*vitatāya*). To the Wide-Spread (*vistīrṇāya*). To the Two-Faced (*dvimukhāya*). To the Three-Faced (*trimukhāya*). Salutation to the Four-Faced (*caturmukhāya*). To the Five-Faced (*pañcamukhāya*). To the Six-Faced (*ṣaṇmukhāya*). To the Downward-Faced (*adhomukhāya*). To the Pervasive *añjali* (*vyāpakāñjalaye*). Salutation to the Cart (*śakaṭāya*). To the [One] with the *sya* [gesture].

Salutation to Yamapāśa; salutation to Dhīgranthikā; salutation to Ma-sammukhonmukha; salutation to Hi-vilamba; salutation to Dhīmuṣṭikā; salutation to Yo-mīna; salutation to Yo-kūrma; salutation to Na-varāha; salutation to Pra-siṃhākrānta; salutation to Co-mahākrānta; salutation to Da-mudgara; salutation to Yā-tpallava.
Then follows breath control (prāṇāyāma).

Of the mantra "Tatsavitur": Viśvāmitra is the seer (ṛṣi); Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ); Savitṛ is the deity (devatā). Its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of recitation (japa) to ward off sins acquired through one's own speech, mind, and body, and for the attainment of the four aims of human life (caturvarga).
Now, meditation.

One should meditate upon Gāyatrī, who possesses three eyes with complexions like pearl, coral, gold, sapphire, and white; who is adorned with a jeweled crown set with the moon; whose essence consists of the principles (tattvas) and the letters of the alphabet; and who holds in her hands the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, a goad, a trident, a skull-cup, and a cord.
I worship her who carries in her hands the conch, the discus, and a pair of lotuses.
(1) Thus: "Come, O Goddess, giver of boons, you who consist of three syllables, expounder of Brahman;
O Gāyatrī, mother of the meters, source of Brahman, salutations be unto you. (3) Thus ends the Gāyatrī.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ; we meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ, who shall inspire our intellects—Oṃ.
Then follows the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma).

The Gāyatrī destroys the sin committed in ten lifetimes with [one recitation], that done in a hundred previous lives with a hundred, and that arising from three ages with a thousand. "O gods, grant passage; O learned ones, O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way. O Lord of the Mind, this..."
"Devayajñaṃ svāhā, vāce svāhā, vāte dhāḥ"—reciting this is the offering; now follows the salutation to the directions.

Oṃ, salutations to the eastern direction and to those deities who dwell therein; and to you, salutations! Salutations to the intermediate direction. (2) Salutations to the southern direction. (3) Salutations to the intermediate direction. (4) Salutations to the western direction. (5) Salutations to the intermediate direction. (6) Salutations to the northern direction. (7)
Homage to the intermediate direction (0). || 8 || Homage to the upward direction (0). || 9 || Homage to the downward direction and those which are [the others] (0).
|| 10 || Homage to Brahman; homage be to Agni; homage to the Earth; homage to the plants. Homage to Speech; homage to the Lord of Speech; homage to the great Viṣṇu I offer. || 3 ||

"Thus, he who, knowing this, studies his own Vedic recitation (svādhyāya), attains proximity to these very deities, as well as equality of power, union, and residence in the same world. Thus is the libation (tarpaṇa).
May all the gods, beginning with Brahmā, be satisfied. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (kaṇṭhopavītī), may all the sages, beginning with Sanaka, be satisfied. 2.
With the sacred thread over the right shoulder: "May all the ancestors, beginning with the Agniṣvātta-s, be satisfied. (3)
Salutation to the deities, to the ancestors, and to the great yogis; salutation to Svāhā and to Svadhā—eternal salutations, salutations again and again.

Oṃ tat sat. Brahmā, today on this lunar day [and so forth], for the sake of the daily obligatory rite (*nityakarman*) of myself, may my father, named so-and-so, of such-and-such lineage (*gotra*), be satisfied with *svadhā*; may he be satisfied, may he be satisfied. [Likewise] the grandfather [2]; the great-grandfather...

Great-grandfather (0); 4. Mother (0); 5. Grandmother (0); 6. Great-grandmother (0); 7. Maternal grandfather (0); 8. Great-uncle (0); 9. Great-great-uncle (0); 10. Maternal grandmother (0); 11. Great-aunt (0); 12. Great-great-aunt (0). In this manner, [one should offer for] all such relatives.
One should satisfy those who belong to the mother’s side, those who are born on the father’s side,
and those who have arisen in the families of one’s teachers, fathers-in-law, and kinsmen.
May all those who have fallen into the state of hungry ghosts (pretas), as well as others who are deprived of funeral offerings (śrāddha), obtain supreme satisfaction through this gift of water.
To all mothers and fathers, and to the twelve ancestral deities, [be] this drink of snow; Svadhā!

The drinking of milk, *svadhā*. The drinking of honey, *svadhā*. Water with sesame seeds, *svadhā*. The libation of water, *svadhā*. Frost, frost. Silver, silver. With the left hand: *Oṃ namo devebhyaḥ*.
With the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*kaṇṭhopavītī*): *Svāhā ṛṣibhyaḥ*. With the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*apasavyena*): *Svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ*. With the left hand.
From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, may the universe—the world with its moving and non-moving beings—be satisfied, be satisfied, be satisfied! May it be so!

Homage to the treasury of Dharma; homage to the witness of one's own deeds; homage to the god manifest before one’s eyes; repeated homage to Bhāskara. By your grace, may there be for me prostration, peace, nourishment, and likewise contentment toward the Sun.
"O King of Tīrthas, may there be the pacification of all sins; salutations unto you. Thus ends the prostration to the Tīrtha.
[Thus ends the procedure for the Sandhyā worship.]
May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
The mantras for the food offering (naivedya). Oṃ [Now, the mantras for the food offering].

Having rendered it nectar-like by means of the Amṛteśaya-mudrā, [one says] "May it be nectar," and having consecrated the food offering as nectar: "The Savitṛ-formulas: By the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, and with the hands of Pūṣan, I take hold of you. To Mahāgaṇapati, to Kumāra, to Śrī, and to Sarasvatī.
To Lakṣmī, to Viśvakarman, to the deities of the door, to Prajāpati, to Brahmā,
to the deities of the water-pot (kalaśa), to the deities Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Maheśvara, to Cāturvedeśvara with his attendants, to Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the Seasons, to Durgā, to Tryambaka, and to Varuṇa.
To the Lord of Sacrifice;
to the hosts of ancestors, the deities of the ancestral sacrifice, beginning with the Agniṣvātta-s; to the Blessed One Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Satya, Puruṣa, and Acyuta.
To Mādhava, to Govinda, to Viṣṇu of a thousand names, to Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Lakṣmī; to the Blessed Lord Bhava, to the God Śarva, to the God Rudra, to the God Paśupati, to the God Ugra,
to the God Bhīma, to Mahādeva, to the God Īśāna, and to Īśvara.
To the god Śiva accompanied by Umā, to the Supreme Lord Pārvatī accompanied by [Śiva],
to the Blessed Vināyaka, the Single-tusked One, the Dark-Tawny One, the Elephant-faced One, the Large-bellied One,
the Crescent-mooned One, Heramba, the Mouse-vehicled One, the Lord of Obstacles, the Consumer of Obstacles.

To Śrī Mahāgaṇeśa, accompanied by his beloved; to Klīṃ-kāra Kumāra, the six-faced one, whose vehicle is the peacock, the commander of the army, Kumāra; to the Blessed One Sūrya, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ, who has seven horses, who is horseless, who has but one horse, whose horses are blue, the manifest deity.

To the Sun, who is the essence of the ultimate truth, whose form is splendor, and who is endowed with radiance; to the Blessed Lady Amā, Kāmā, Cārvaṅgī, Ṭaṅkadhāriṇī, Tārā, Pārvatī, Yakṣiṇī, the Blessed Lady Śrī-Śārikā,
the Blessed Lady Śrī-Śāradā, and the Blessed Lady Śrī-Mahārājñī.
To the Blessed Śrījvālā, to the Blessed Vrīḍā, to the Blessed Vaikharī, to the Blessed Vitastā, to the Blessed Gaṅgā, to the Blessed Yamunā, to the Blessed Kālikā, to Siddhalakṣmī, to Mahālakṣmī,
to Mahātripurasundarī, to the Goddess of a Thousand Names, to Bhavānī, and to the Goddess Abhayaṃkarī.

To the Blessed Lady Kṣemaṃkarī, the destroyer of all enemies; to Bhairava, the sovereign of this kingdom; to Indra, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand; to Agni, who holds a spear in his hand; to Yama, who holds a staff in his hand; to Nairṛti, who holds a sword in his hand; to Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand; to Vāyu, who holds a banner in his hand; to Kubera...
To Īśāna who holds a mace in his hand; to Brahmā who holds a trident in his hand; to Viṣṇu who holds a discus in his hand;
to the eight Kula-nāga deities beginning with Ananta;
and to Agni and Āditya, Varuṇa and Candramas, Kumāra and Bhauma.
To Viṣṇu and Budha; to Indra and Bṛhaspati; to Sarasvatī and Śukra; to Prajāpati and Śanaiścara; to Gaṇapati and Rāhu; to Rudra and Ketu;
to Brahmā and Dhruva; to Ananta and Agastya; and to Brahmā, Kūrma, and Dhruva.
To Ananta and Hari; to Lakṣmī and Kamalā; to the forty-five deities of the Vāstoṣpati sacrifice, beginning with Śikhin; to the Mothers beginning with Brāhmī;
to the Mothers beginning with Gaurī; to the Mothers beginning with Lalitā.
To the deities of the Durgā-kṣetra and Gaṇeśvara; to the deities of Rākā; to the deities of Trikā;

to the deities of Sinīvālī; to the deities of Yāmī; to the deities of Raudrī; to the deities of Vāruṇī; to the deities of Bārhaspatya; *oṃ* to the deities of Bhūḥ; *oṃ* to the deities of Bhuvaḥ; *oṃ*.
To the deities of the three worlds: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, to the deities of the three worlds;
to the deities of the sacrifice of the undivided cosmic egg; to the Dhurs and Upadhurs;
to Mahāgāyatrī, Sāvitrī, and Sarasvatī; to Herakā and the others; to Vaṭuka and the others.
This divine nectar was produced before the churning of the Ocean of Milk;
please accept this food offering as the form of that nectar.

Having recited the meditation on the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatādhyāna*) and [the mantra] beginning with *tatsad brahma*, [one says]: "For the sake of such-and-such a rite, *oṃ namo naivedyaṃ nivedayāmi namaḥ*."
Whatever yoginīs there may be—whether fierce, gentle, most terrible, or supreme;
whether moving in the sky, moving on the earth, or beautiful maidens—may they always be pleased with me.
To the Ākāśa-mothers, food: obeisance. To the Ākāśa-mothers, the application of unguent:

fragrance: obeisance. Water for the guest-offering: obeisance. Flowers: obeisance. Having meditated upon the chosen deity, I offer—obeisance—to [Name] Deva this milk-rice, sweetmeats, cooked food, cakes, or other food, and so forth.
To that guardian of the field who dwells in this sacred precinct,
together with his attendants, I today offer this oblation accompanied by water.
"KṢĀM! To the Lord of the Field, food, obeisance! RĀM! To the Lord of the Realm, food, obeisance!
O Bestower of all fearlessness and boons, may the Lord of Nourishment bestow nourishment upon me! I am fallen [into distress]; You are the refuge;
always, in all circumstances... and so forth. Having thus offered flowers for forgiveness, with both knees...
With both hands, with my head, with my chest, and with my mind, I offer salutation; *namaḥ*.
"Salutation to Brahman"—this is the libation (*tarpaṇa*).
[Thus ends the ritual procedure for the mantra of the food offering (*naivedya*):]
Oṃ. Now, [the ritual procedure for the worship of the fivefold abode of Viṣṇu].

Oṃ. Of this mantra for purifying the seat (āsana-śodhana), Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi), Sutala is the meter (chandaḥ), and Kūrma is the deity (devatā). It is employed for the purification of the seat. Homage to Merupṛṣṭha, the seer, upon the head; to Sutala...
Salutation to *chandas* on the face; salutation to the deity Kūrma on the heart; salutation to the *viniyoga* for the purification of the seat on all limbs.
O Earth, you uphold the worlds; O Goddess, you are upheld by Viṣṇu. Therefore, O Goddess, support me and make this seat pure.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, and firm are these mountains;
firm is this entire world, and you, O King, are the firm one of the people.

Thus ends the seating. *Prīṃ*. To the Earth, to the Support-Power (*Ādhāraśakti*): salutation with fragrant unguent; salutation with the water-offering (*argha*); salutation with flowers. Then, the prostration.
For the pacification of all obstacles, one should meditate upon the God who wears white garments, who is moon-colored, four-armed, and has a gracious countenance. (1)
Salutations to that Lord of the Gaṇas, who is worshipped even by the gods for the sake of accomplishing desired aims, and who cuts through all obstacles. || 2 ||
Blessed are they, victorious are they; how could there be defeat for those in whose hearts dwells Janārdana, dark as a blue lotus?
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is Maheśvara himself;
the Guru alone is the entire universe—salutations to that venerable Guru. 4.
O Goddess of great strength and great energy, destroyer of great fear!
Protect me, O Goddess who are difficult for enemies to behold and the increaser of their terror. (5)

Oṃ, homage to the Guru; homage to the Supreme Guru; homage to the Preceptor Parameṣṭhin; homage to the Supreme Teacher; homage to the Primordial Siddhas. Oṃ, "without beginning," and so forth. Having performed the *pṛthak* [separation] ending with "Oṃ, Brahma, Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Oṃ" at the head, [one recites] "Oṃ, that supreme step of Viṣṇu" at the heart. They always behold it...

The wise ones [meditate] upon it with their heads; like an eye stretched across the sky, they meditate upon it with their tufts of hair; the inspired poets, praising it, being ever-watchful, kindle it with their voices; that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu, they meditate upon it with their weapons. Rudra who is in the fire, they meditate upon him with their hearts; he who is in the waters, he who is in the plants, they meditate upon him with their heads; he who is in the lords of the forest, he who is Rudra in all beings... they meditate upon him with their tufts of hair.

He entered the armor (*kavaca*). To that Rudra, [I offer] the eye (*netra*). Homage be to the gods; *phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*). We invoke you, Gaṇapati, the lord of hosts (*gaṇa*), the sage (*kavi*) among sages, the most highly renowned, the sovereign king of sacred formulations (*brahman*), O Lord of Brahmans (*brahmaṇaspati*). Hearing us with your aids, [protect us]. *Gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ havāmahe kaviṃ kavīnāṃ upamaśravastamaṃ śikhā jyeṣṭharājaṃ brahmaṇāṃ brahmaṇas pate ā naḥ śṛṇvan ūtibhiḥ.* [The mantra for the head (*śikhā*) is: "We invoke you, the lord of hosts among hosts, the sage among sages, the one of most exalted fame, the supreme king of sacred formulations, O Lord of Brahmans; hearing us, come to us with your protections. [The mantra for the hair-tuft (*kaca*) is: "O Lord of Brahmans... [The mantra for the eyes (*netra*) is: "Hearing us with your aids... [The mantra for the armor (*kavaca*) is: "He entered the armor... [The mantra for the weapon (*astra*) is: "Homage be to the gods; *phaṭ* to the weapon!"

*Sīda* is on the seat; *sādanam* on the feet; *citram* on the two feet; *devānām* on the shanks; *udgāt* on the knees; *anīkam* on the thighs; *cakṣuḥ* on the penis; *mitrasya* on the private parts; *varuṇasya* on the navel; *agneḥ* on the heart;
*āprā dyāvāpṛthivī* on the throat; *antarikṣam* on the arms; *sūryaḥ* on the mouth; *ātmā* [on the self].
In the nose of that which moves; in the eyes of that which stands still; on the forehead and on the head;

born on the crest; for the Veda on the forehead; "we shall press" on the ears; "Soma" on the nose; "the enemy" on the two eyes; "from whence" on the two lips; "down" on the teeth; "he burns" on the palate; "he knows" on the tongue; "he" on the neck; "of us."

*Parṣat* in the two arms; *ati* in the heart; *dur* in the two breasts; *gāṇi* in the belly; *viśvā* on the back; *nāva* in the two hands; *iva* in the two thighs; *sindhum* in the penis; *dur* in the hips; *itaḥ* in the two thighs; *ati* in the two shanks; *agniḥ* in the two feet. While scattering sesame seeds in all directions.

May those beings depart who are stationed upon the earth; may those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva. May those beings who dwell on the earth or in the intermediate space, and those who have gone to the world of heaven, who indeed cause harm with their nooses—[depart].
May those wicked ones perish by the command of Śiva. One should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) and bathe in the sacred water (tīrtha), reciting:
"Thou art the purifier of Vasu, with a hundred streams; thou art the purifier of Vasus, with a thousand streams.
Free from disease, I unite you with progeny; becoming abundant, may you increase in wealth. Thus.
The holding of the purifier (pavitra) is for the Supreme Self, the Puruṣottama, whose nature consists of the five elements, the Self of the universe,
the Lord of Mantras, the Self as Nārāyaṇa, and the Support-Power (Ādhāra-śakti); [this is] the fragrant unguent.
"Obeisance! Water for the feet! Obeisance! Flower! Obeisance!"—with these words, one offers the scents and other articles to one's own self.
"The great lamp, self-luminous, which dispels darkness on all sides;
be gracious to me, O Govinda; this lamp has been prepared for you."

This divine incense, the essence of the forest trees, rich in fragrance and most excellent among scents, is prepared as an invocation for all the gods. Homage to the treasury of Dharma; homage to the witness of one's own deeds.
Homage to the god who is directly perceived, to Bhāskara; salutations again and again!
Where there is no mother, no father, no kinsman, and where even no brother or friend exists;
where neither day nor night is known—there I take refuge in the lamp of the Self.

May there be success through the resolve for incense and lamp for myself, Nārāyaṇa, and Ādhāra-śakti; obeisance to the incense, obeisance to the lamp. Oṃ tat sat brahma (0). To Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the Seasons, in Mārgaśīrṣa, to Kṛṣṇa accompanied by Rukmiṇī, to Keśava accompanied by Śrī; in Pauṣa...
To Ananta, the Lord of Speech (Vāgīśvara), and Nārāyaṇa, [be there] love in the month of Māgha;
to Acyuta and Kānta, [be there] joy in Māgha; to Cakrin and Govinda, [be there] power in Phālguna;
to Vaikuṇṭha and Viṣṇu, [be there] accomplishment in Caitra; to Janārdana, [be there] splendor in Vaiśākha.
To Madhusūdana, [offering] *vibhūti* in the month of Jyeṣṭha; to Upendra, *mahiman* in Āṣāḍha; to Trivikrama, *icchā* in Śrāvaṇa; to Yajñapuruṣa, *lakṣmī* in Bhādrapada;
to Vāmana, *dhṛti* in Āśvina; to Vāsudeva, *kānti* in Kārttika; to Śrīdhara, *rati* in Mārgaśīrṣa; and to Hari, *prāpti* in Pauṣa.

To Hṛṣīkeśa, [offering] Māyā in the month of Āśvayuja; to Yogīśvara, [offering] Prākāmyā; to Padmanābha, [offering] Dhī; to Puṇḍarīkākṣa, [offering] Laghimā in the month of Kārtika; to Dāmodara, [offering] Garimā;
to Narakāri, [offering] Satyabhāmā in the intercalary month (Malimluca); and to Mahāmārtāṇḍa and Durgā, [offering] Niṣkalā.
And so forth. To the thousand-named Goddess Bhavānī, [and] to the deities of the five abodes of Viṣṇu:

*namaḥ* to incense, *namaḥ* to the lamp. With the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*apasavya*), *namaḥ* to the ancestors: for the sake of the daily rite, to the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather; to the mother, grandmother, and great-grandmother.

To the maternal grandfather, the great maternal grandfather, and the great-great maternal grandfather; to the maternal grandmother, the great maternal grandmother, and the great-great maternal grandmother;
to all the ancestors, the twelve deities, and the paternal ancestors—incense, *svadhā*; lamp, *svadhā*. (With the sacred thread over the left shoulder.)
I unite your heart; may your mind be united with the vital breaths. || 1 ||
May your bodies be united; may your breath be united. || 2 ||
May your beloved bodies be ours, may your hearts be dear to us; may your souls be dear to us, and may our bodies be dear to you. 3.

Having thus cast three flowers into the water-vessel, the bestowing of life for the deity should be performed with the mantra: "The breath of the Aśvins—may those two grant you breath; by that, live! The breath of Mitra and Varuṇa—may those two grant you breath; by that, live! The breath of Bṛhaspati—may he grant you breath; by that, live!"

One should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) upon the body of the deity as follows: *oṃ a* at the navel, and so forth. Then, one should perform the invocation (*āvāhana*): *oṃ bhūḥ puruṣam*, etc.

*oṃ bhūḥ puruṣam āvāhayāmi namaḥ* (I invoke the Puruṣa of the Earth; obeisance). *oṃ bhuvaḥ puruṣam āvāhayāmi namaḥ* (I invoke the Puruṣa of the Atmosphere; obeisance). *oṃ svaḥ puruṣam āvāhayāmi namaḥ* (I invoke the Puruṣa of Heaven; obeisance). *oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ puruṣam āvāhayāmi namaḥ* (I invoke the Puruṣa of the Earth, Atmosphere, and Heaven; obeisance). (3)

Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ tat sat (0) || 3 || Homage be to Ananta || 3 || We know Vāsudeva; we meditate upon Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa; may that Viṣṇu inspire us || 3 || Victory is yours, O lotus-eyed one; homage to you, O creator of the universe! Homage be to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Great Person!
O First-born! || 3 || Oṃ, salutations to the dwarf who is the cause, to the benefactor of cows and Brahmins;

salutations again and again to Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, the benefactor of the world. || 3 || We know Him as the Universal Form (Viśvarūpa); we meditate upon Viṣvaksena; may that Viṣṇu inspire us. || 3 || [Salutations] to Narasiṃha, for the crossing over of the hellish realm... for wisdom (dhī). || 3 ||
May Viṣṇu grant that to us. (Gāyatrī mantra for Viṣṇu) To Tatpuruṣa, to Mahādeva, may we meditate; may Śiva grant that to us. (Gāyatrī mantra for Śiva)
Tatpuruṣāya vidmahe, vikṛtatuṇḍāya dhīmahi, tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt || 3 || Bhāskarāya vidmahe,

sahasraraśmaye dhīmahi, tannaḥ sūryaḥ pracodayāt || 3 || Subhagāyai vidmahe, kāmamālinyai dhīmahi, tanno durgā pracodayāt || 3 || Oṃ tat sad brahma... [and so forth] of the Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Seasons.
Of Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Satya, Puruṣa,
Acyuta, Mādhava, Govinda, Viṣṇu of a thousand names, Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Lakṣmī; and of the Blessed Lord Bhava, the god Śarva, the god Rudra, the god...
To the Lord Paśupati, the fierce god, the formidable god, Mahādeva, the sovereign god Īśāna, the lord god Īśvara, to Śiva accompanied by Umā, to the Supreme Lord accompanied by Pārvatī;
to the Blessed Vināyaka, the one-tusked, the dark-brown, the elephant-faced, the pot-bellied.
To Bhālacandra, Heramba, Ākhuratha, Vighneśa, Vighnabhakṣya,
and Śrī Mahāgaṇeśa together with his beloved; to the Blessed Sūrya, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ,
who possesses seven horses, no horses, one horse, and blue horses.
Of the manifest deity, the essence of ultimate reality, the form of splendor, the radiant Āditya;
of the Blessed Lady Amāyā, Kāmā, Cārvaṅgī, Ṭakadhāriṇī, Tārā, Pārvatī, Yakṣiṇī, the Blessed Śrīśārikā, and Śrīśāradā...

To the illustrious Mahārājñī, to the illustrious Jvālābhā, Vīḍābhā, Vaikharībhā, Vitastābhā, Gaṅgābhā, Yamunābhā, Kālikābhā, to Siddhalakṣmī, to Mahālakṣmī, to Mahātripurasundarī, to the Goddess whose names are a thousandfold, to Bhavānī.
For the sake of pleasing Śrī Viṣṇu, I shall perform the worship of the five-deity assembly (pañcāyatana) of Viṣṇu, [or] of myself, through speech, mind, and body; Oṃ, do so.
Having scattered sesame, mustard seeds, and barley, [he performs] the offering of the seat with the mantra beginning, "The Person alone is this... the firm heaven...
[and] "This is the seat for the Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Lord Vāsudeva, the Lord of the Seasons," etc.;
[saying] "Salutation to you"—to the Lord of the Seasons, to Nārāyaṇa, to the Lord Vāsudeva, and so forth. To you all:

I worship: Oṃ, worship! "The thousand-headed... [Sahasraśīrṣā Puruṣa Sūkta]. "The wise ones harness the mind and they harness their thoughts, the inspired poets of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, knowing the ways, ordains the priestly functions; this is the praise of the divine Savitṛ. "That of Viṣṇu... [Tad Viṣṇoḥ Paramam Padam]. To the Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Lord Vāsudeva, the Lord of Cosmic Order (Ṛtupati).
To Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Satya, Puruṣa, Acyuta, Mādhava, Govinda, Viṣṇu of a thousand names, Nārāyaṇa together with Lakṣmī; and to the Blessed Lord Bhava-deva,
Śarva-deva, Rudra-deva, Paśupati-deva, and Ugra-deva.
To Bhīmadeva, Mahādeva, Īśānadeva, Īśvaradeva, Śiva accompanied by Umā,
Parameśvara accompanied by Pārvatī, the Blessed Vināyaka, Ekadanta, Kṛṣṇapiṅgala, Gajānana, Lambodara, Bhālacandra, Heramba, and Ākhuratha.
To Vighneśa, the devourer of obstacles, accompanied by his beloved, the illustrious Mahāgaṇeśa;

to the Blessed One Sūrya— Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ— the one with seven horses, the horseless, the one-horsed, the blue-horsed, the manifest deity, the essence of the supreme truth, whose form is splendor, Āditya together with Prabhā.
To the Blessed One, Amā, Kāmā, Cārvaṅgī, Ṭaṅkadhāriṇī, Tārā, Pārvatī, Yakṣiṇī, the Blessed Śrī Śārikā, Śrī Śāradāmbā,
Śrī Mahārājñī, Śrī Jvālāmbā, Vrīḍāmbā, Vaikharī, Vitastāmbā, Gaṅgāmbā, and Yamunāmbā.
I shall invoke Kālikā, Siddhalakṣmī, Mahālakṣmī, Mahātripurasundarī,
the Goddess whose names are a thousand, Bhavānī, and the deities of the Viṣṇu-pañcāyatana:
Oṃ, invoke!
I invoke the Lord of Lakṣmī, whose pair of feet are praised by hosts of immortals, the cause of the universe, the immeasurable,
the primordial one with eternal form, seated upon the seat of the Praṇava.
Having the form of a thousand full moons, suns, and fires. || 1 ||
One should meditate upon the Supreme, the most venerable among those who know all principles,
whose forms are gentle as the Boar, Kapila, and the Man-lion,
and whose limbs are adorned with the Śrīvatsa mark and the great Kaustubha jewel.
Holding in his hands the Kaumodakī mace, the lotus, the conch, and the discus. || 2 ||
O Blessed One, although you are indeed all-pervading, I nevertheless invoke you just as one fans the wind with a fan;
for just as fire, though hidden, emerges through friction, so too do you approach when invoked.
And [I shall] worship. || 3 ||

O Mālādhara, O Acyuta, O All-pervading Lord, O Supreme Self in embodied form, O Omniscient One, O Protector, O Supreme Sovereign, O Omnipotent One! Come to me, show me compassion, accept this image, and receive my worship.
Today, with the desire to bestow grace upon me. || 4 ||
I invoke Hari, who resembles a jewel, seated within the lotus of the heart in the city of Māyā within my own reflection;
having offered the ritual bath with water purified by the river of faith, I worship Him according to the rite of the eight flowers of devotion.

I salute him who has the luster of cow’s milk, whose eyes are as long as lotuses, whose limbs are adorned with ornaments such as the parasol and horse, who is worshipped by Śrī and Bhūmi, who is established in the yoga-seat, and who is honored by the Lotus-born Brahmā. 6.

I invoke Viṣṇu, who is luminous, dwelling within all beings, known as Oṃkāra, attainable through meditation by yogins, eternally served by his own powerful limbs and weapons, and possessing all forms. (6) [Of Śiva]
O Śiva, enemy of Tripura! O Lord of all, who pervades the universe! Out of compassion for this devotee, remain as a pillar [in this] linga for even a single moment;
having ascended the lotus of my heart, O Blessed One, accept the worship offered by me.
I am pleased with you today. || 7 ||
Of Gaṇeśa:
O son of Śaileśvara, O child, you who hold a staff, an axe, and a noose in your hands for the sake of destroying the obstacles of your devotees!
O Lord of the Gate, leader of all the hosts, lotus-handed one, accept this worship; O Blessed One, be pleased with me today! || 1 ||
O Sun, illuminator of the mansion of the universe, embodiment of Śambhu, treasury of splendor, lord of the sky-dwellers, primordial deity!
O Blessed One, accept today this worship performed by me according to the rite of all offerings; be present for me today.
He was satisfied. || 1 ||
O Durgā! O Śrī Śāradā! O best of goddesses! O Tripurā! O Mistress of the gods! O Durgā! O Bhavānī! O Vaikharī, Mother of the Universe! Indeed!
O you who dwell in the half-body of Śarva, accompanied by your retinue, accept this worship; O fortunate one, be pleased with me today! || 1 ||
O Blessed One, lotus-eyed one, bestower of grace upon devotees, O Lord, out of compassion for us, please remain present here.
Having thus addressed Gāyatrī and recited it three times, the knower of reality should worship the deity within his own self with mentally conceived offerings; then,
having projected that form of radiant energy into the image, he should worship once again.
Having scattered barley grains, one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma); [the formula for] the water for washing the feet is "namaḥ."

"Śanno devī... [The mantra]. Poppy seeds, saffron, along with all medicinal herbs, sprouts of *darbha* grass, and water—these five components constitute the characteristics of the *pādya* (water for washing the feet).
"Venerable sirs, here is the *pādya*, the *pādya*. 2.

This much is for him [the guest]: the four verses beginning with *hiraṇyavarṇāḥ*. The water for the feet (*pādya*) is offered with the mantra beginning with *ṛtupataye*, followed by *namaḥ*. Having set aside the remainder, one again recites *śanno devīḥ*. Water, milk, tips of *kuśa* grass, clarified butter, curd, rice grains, barley, and white mustard seeds—this is indeed called the eightfold *arghya*.
Venerable ones, this is the water of honor. 2.
Three-quarters above. Pṛthivī. Oṃ āpo hi ṣṭhā. Ṛtupate Nārāyaṇa, Blessed One Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Satya, Puruṣa, Acyuta, Mādhava, Govinda, Sahasranāman Viṣṇu!

O Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Lakṣmī! O Blessed One, Bhavadeva, Śarvadeva, Rudradeva, Paśupati, Deva, Ugradeva, Bhīmadeva, Mahādeva, Īśānadeva, Īśvaradeva, Śiva accompanied by Umā, Parameśvara accompanied by Pārvatī! O Blessed Vināyaka, Ekadanta, Kṛṣṇapiṅgala, Gajānana!

O Lambodara, Bhālacandra, Heramba, Ākhuratha, Vighneśa, Vighnabhakṣa; O Śrī Mahāgaṇeśa, together with your beloved! O Blessed One, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ; O Sūrya, Saptāśva, Anaśva, Ekāśva, Nīlāśva; O Pratyakṣadeva, Paramārthasāra, Tejorūpa; O Āditya, together with Prabhā! O Blessed Lady!

O Amā, O Kāmā, O Cārvaṅgī, O Ṭaṅkadhāriṇī, O Tārā, O Pārvatī, O Yakṣiṇī, O Blessed Śrī-Śārikā, O Śrī-Śāradā, O Śrī-Mahārājñī, O Śrī-Jvālā, O Vrīḍā, O Vaikharī, O Vitastā, O Gaṅgā, O Yamunā, O Kālikā, O Siddhalakṣmī, O Mahālakṣmī!

O Mahātripurasundarī, O Goddess Sahasranāmnī, O Bhavānī, O deities of the Viṣṇupañcāyatana, this *arghya* is for you; salutations! To Virāṭ, Pṛśni, Śannāpaḥ, Pṛśni, Ṛtupati, and the others, water for sipping (*ācamanīya*) is offered; salutations! [To those addressed by] "yat puruṣeṇa," "pṛśni," "imam āpaḥ," "pṛśni," and "ṛtupati," [water for sipping is offered]; salutations!
From these [mantras], [the water] for the ritual bath is offered with the salutation "namas."
Now, the twenty-one ablutions:

milk, curd, ghee, honey, parched grain, white mustard seeds, sesame seeds, barley, rice, kuśa grass, dūrvā grass, earth, ashes, fruit, sugar, the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), camphor, and medicinal herbs; these are the twenty-one ablutions, as well as fragrant flowers.

O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one. Then, O Āditya, under your law, may we be sinless before Aditi. May there be milk on the earth, milk in the plants, milk in the heavens, and milk bestowed in the mid-air; may the quarters of space be full of milk for me. 1.

Of Dadhikrāvan: The two possessors of ghee, the protectors of beings, the wide and vast, the earth that yields sweetness and is well-formed—Heaven and Earth, by the law of Varuṇa, are held apart, ageless and rich in seed.
Sweet are the winds for the one who follows the Truth; sweet do the rivers flow. May the plants be full of sweetness for us. Sweet...
May the night and the dawns be honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be honey-sweet; may our Father Heaven be honey-sweet.
May the Lord of the Forest be honey-sweet for us, and may Sūrya be honey-sweet. May our cows be full of sweetness. 9.

The three deities, acting in harmony through their powers, bestowed upon him that immortal form: the blades of grass became his hair in many ways, the young sprouts his skin, and the parched grains became his flesh. || 5 ||
I sprinkle the slayer of demons, the vigorous one; I approach the friend for the sake of the most extensive protection.

May Agni, sharpened by our rites and kindled, who hastens from heaven, protect us by night. You are sesame, having Soma as your deity, produced by the gods at the Gosava sacrifice; O vital breath, come to the worlds of the ancestors with those who are diligent.
Svadhā! || 7 || You are barley; barter away our enemies, barter away the stingy one. I strew you upon the world that is the seat of the ancestors. || 8 || You are grain;
satisfy the gods, satisfy the sacrifice, satisfy the lord of the sacrifice, and satisfy this sacrifice. || 9 || [I take] you of the god...
At the impulse of Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take it up. || 10 ||

Growing from joint to joint, rising from every stalk—thus, O *dūrvā* grass, spread for us with a thousandfold and a hundredfold increase. Having stepped upon the earth, O steed, seek the fire with your luster;
having entered the earth, tell us our path, so that we may dig for you there. Having become tranquil through the ashes...

Having united with the womb, the waters, and the earth of Agni, you, radiant with light, have settled down again with your mothers. May those plants that bear fruit and those that are unfruitful, those that are sheathed and those that are un-sheathed,
being impelled by Bṛhaspati, release us from sin.

With pebbles he [overcomes] the Avakā plant, and with Avakā plants the pebble; with the Avakrandana [hymn] the tongue, and with Sarasvatī the palate at the tip of the tongue. The five dawns follow the cow that milks five times;
the five seasons follow her who has five names. The five directions are fashioned by the fifteenfold [stoma].

They have a common head and look toward a single goal. Having mixed cow’s urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and water from *kuśa* grass, the honeyed wave from the ocean has attained immortality through the low-voiced chant (*upāṃśu*). That which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue.

The navel of immortality for the gods. (17) We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the nourisher of wealth; may I be released from death, as a cucumber from its stem, but not from immortality. (18) Those herbs which were born first, three ages before the gods—of those brown ones, I take the essence. (19)
One hundred and seven abodes. (19) I invoke here Śrī, who has fragrance as her door, who is unassailable, eternally nourishing, and bestowing abundance; she is the sovereign of all beings.
(20) The plants that bear flowers, those that yield fruit, those that are fruitful, and even those that are fruitless—may they carry us across [to safety], like victorious mares. (21)
"Obeisance to the Lord of the Seasons (*Ṛtupati*), and so forth"—with these [mantras], perform twenty-one ritual ablutions (*snāna*). Oṃ, obeisance!
With water, milk, curd, ghee, honey, barley, sugar, mustard seeds, sesame, and likewise with gold, camphor, saffron, parched grain, walnuts, and flowers.

Then, one should offer all medicinal herbs and water for the sixteen baths of Viṣṇu. One should present the sixteen baths to Viṣṇu with the sixteen verses beginning with "Vasoḥ pavitram asi" and "Ṛtupataye," followed by water poured in a hundred streams with the mantra "Namaḥ."
"Salutation to the water of a thousand streams. Then, with the *Puruṣasūkta* beginning with "Of the Anuṣṭubh... [and reciting the sixteen verses]. [Verse 1:

"The goddess who was born as Indra’s fortunate consort—she, being in harmony with splendor, has arrived here: she who is in the elephant, in the leopard, in the prize of the bull, in the wind, in Parjanya, and in the might of Varuṇa. [Verse 2: "She who is in the elephant, in the leopard..."

That splendor which is in gold, in cows, in horses, and within men—[that] Indra, [I invoke]. (2) The splendor which is in the lion, in the tiger, and also in the viper, in fire, in the sacred word (*brahman*), and in the sun—[that] divine one, [I invoke] Indra. (3) The splendor which is in the noble warrior (*rājanya*), in the stretched drum, in the leaping of the horse, and in the magic power (*māyā*) of man—[that] Indra... (4) thus.
With the Lakṣmīsūkta and "Tad Viṣṇoḥ," and so forth with "Ṛtupataye," [one performs] the sixteen baths; obeisance.

Thus, one should always perform [ablutions] with excellent substances: with water interspersed with milk, curd, ghee, honey, sugarcane juice, and medicinal herbs; with rice-water, flower-water, fruit-water, and water with white mustard and parched grain; and with fragrant water containing auspicious gold and jewels.

One should offer the fifteen great ablutions (*mahāsnāna*) to Śambhu in sequence along with water: (1) *ud uttamaṃ*, (2) *payas pṛthivyāḥ*, (3) *dadhi krāvṇo*, (4) *ghṛtavatī*, (5) *madhuvātā*. [And: "Sweet for the divine race, sweet for Indra whose names are easy to invoke, sweet for Mitra and Varuṇa."
To Vāyu and Bṛhaspati, [this] honeyed, inviolable [oblation]. (6) The plants... (7) You are grain.

(8) Those that have flowers, (9) those that bear fruit. (10) The Rakṣas-slayer. (11) That is his form. (12) O Goddess whose door is fragrance. (13) Gold-colored ones. (14) Right and Truth. (15) Pṛ... (7) Innumerable.
The thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth—for them we unbend our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.

(1) Those who are in this great ocean, in the intermediate space—for them... (2) Those blue-necked, white-throated Rudras who have taken refuge in heaven—for them... (3) Those blue-necked, white-throated ones...
And those who move upon the earth below, O Śarva; those who dwell in the forests as craftsmen, blue-necked and deep red.

Those who pierce through the food and drink from the vessels of men—those [I invoke]. Those who are the lords of beings, hairless yet wearing matted locks—those [I invoke]. Those who guard the paths, who scatter the devourers of the *iḍā* offering—those [I invoke]. Those who frequent the sacred fords, armed with spears—those [I invoke].
The quiver-bearers—those [Rudras] who, whether they be this many or even more, have spread themselves through the quarters. Those [Rudras]...

(10) || Oṃ! Let there be homage to the Rudras who are in heaven, whose arrows are the rain; to them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten above—let there be homage to them. May they be gracious to us.
Whomsoever we hate, and whosoever hates us, him I place within their jaws. (1) || Oṃ! Let there be homage.

To the Rudras who are in the intermediate space, whose arrows are the wind—to them, ten [fingers] toward the east. (2) Om! Homage be to the Rudras who are on earth, whose arrows are food—to them. (3) The Rudra who is in fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants, who is in the trees; the Rudra who has entered all beings—to that Rudra, homage.

"May it be so, O gods! To the Blessed Lord Bhava, the god," and so forth—these are the fifteen ablutions; [to each] "namas. Oṃ, we invoke you, Gaṇapati, the lord of hosts, the sage among sages, possessed of the highest renown, the eldest king of the sacred hymns, O Lord of Prayer (Brahmaṇaspati); hearing us, sit upon your seat with your protections.
"Salutations to the Blessed Vināyaka," and so forth— these are the fourteen ablutions. Milk, curd, ghee, sugarcane juice,
sesame seeds, barley, honey, parched grain, nectar, the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*),
as well as perfumes, flowers, and medicinal herbs— these are declared by the wise to be for the thirteen ablutions of the Sun.

With the six verses beginning with *udvayaṃ tamasas pari*, [and] *pṛ*... *paṃ*... *hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya* and so forth, there are thirteen ablutions; [ending with] *namaḥ*. For the bath of the Goddess, one should prepare parched grain (*lāja*), fragrance, *vācaḥ*, *kuṣṭha*, *vāluka*, *śaṅkhapuṣpaka*, saffron (*kuṅkuma*), agallochum (*aguru*), and camphor (*karpūra*). I...
I move with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas.
I sustain both Mitra and Varuṇa; I [sustain] Indra and Agni, and I [sustain] both the Aśvins. Dadhikrā, the Dark One, the Waters...

Hiṣṭhā (0). Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ (0). Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas, so that he may burn away the wealth of the stingy enemy. May Agni carry us across all difficulties and beyond all evils, as one crosses a river with a boat. [Offer] the eight ablutions beginning with "To the Blessed Amā" and ending with "Namaḥ. Agni is the Ṛṣi, Pavamāna.

We pray to that Pañcajanya, the domestic priest of great wealth. Salutation to the bath for the conch Pañcajanya. By what [means] has the wonderful one become our messenger? He is the friend who ever increases us; by what most powerful [means] is he encompassed?
Salutation to the bath for the divine bell, the messenger of the gods. Then...

"May all the gods, beginning with Brahmā, be satisfied," and so forth—this is the libation for the divine seers (*devarṣi*) and ancestors (*pitṛ*). With the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*savya*), one who recites this libation on the Viṣṇu-seat or the auspicious seat (*bhadrapīṭha*) shall enjoy wealth, fame, renown, and constant happiness; and the sacrificer shall have long life and many sons.

May he always obtain a body that is pure and sanctified, the eternal fruit of the gift of a cow. May there be no obstacle for me, may there be no sin; may those who stand as adversaries be gentle, and may the *bhūtas* and *pretas* be satisfied and bringers of happiness. *Oṃ namo devebhyaḥ*, etc. [With pure water, the mantra] *tad viṣṇoḥ*...

Salutation to the *mantra-guḍaka* beginning with "To the Blessed One" (*bhagavate vā*) and so forth. *Oṃ pratyaṅgne harasāharaḥ śṛṇīhi viśvataḥ prati | yātudhānasya rakṣaso balaṃ viruja vīryam ||* (This is for the *ārātrikā*.
"We desire to go to those dwellings of yours where the many-horned, swift cows are. Herein—
"That supreme station of the wide-striding Bull shines forth abundantly. Thus is the touching of the eyes.

Water, sandalwood paste, the discus, the conch, a *tulasī* leaf, a bell, a stone, and a copper leaf—this is the eightfold nectar of the feet (*caraṇāmṛta*). "Oṃ tad viṣṇoḥ... "To the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva," and so forth.

I receive the nectar from [your] feet; salutations! One should sprinkle water on the head with the mantra *āpo hi ṣṭhā*. Salutations to the seat; salutations to the lotus seat; salutations to the Garuḍa seat; salutations to the hundred-petaled lotus seat; salutations to the thousand-petaled lotus seat; salutations to the bull seat; salutations to the rat seat; salutations to the seven-horse seat; salutations to the lion seat.

Arise, O Blessed Viṣṇu! Arise, O Lord of Kamalā! Arise, O Lord of the three worlds! Bestow auspiciousness upon the three realms! Having recited the *Mukundamālā*, [one applies] unguent to the axle and other parts of the chariot with the mantra: *Oṃ bhagavate vāsudevāya* (and so forth), ending with *...gṛhṇāmi namaḥ*. [One then recites: *taṃ yajñaṃ yuvā...*

"To Suvāsas (the well-clothed one), to the Lord of Seasons," and so forth—to these [deities], [I offer] clothing; *namaḥ*. From that sacrifice, from which all is offered, was gathered the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*); "the sacred thread of the season"—to the garment, *namaḥ*.
From that sacrifice, from which all is offered, [were gathered] the *ṛc* verses; "that which has fragrance as its door" (*gandhadvārām*), "of the season"—[this is] the anointing, the fragrance.

*Namaḥ*. Therefore, [offer] the horse (*aśva*), the flowering one (*puṣpavatī*), the season (*ṛtu*), and the water-offering (*argha*). *Namaḥ*. [Offer] the flower (*puṣpa*). Then, with the *Puruṣasūkta* and the *Lakṣmīsūkta*, [worship]: *namaḥ* to Nārāyaṇa in the east; to Puṇḍarīkākṣa in the south; to Govinda in the west; to Madhusūdana in the north; and in the northeast—

To Viṣṇu in the east, to Janārdana in the southeast, to Padmanābha in the southwest, to Vāmana in the northwest, to Vāsudeva above, to Lokanātha below, to Keśava in the center, and to the conch, the discus, the mace, the plow, and the pestle.
To Kaustubha, Jaya, Vijaya, Dhātrī, Śeṣa, and the two solstices; at the door, to Caṇḍa and Upacaṇḍa;
to the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, and Atharvaveda; to the Kṛta Age, Tretā Age, Dvāpara Age, and Kali Age; Oṃ, to Bhūrloka, Oṃ, to Bhuvarloka, Oṃ, to Svarloka, Oṃ, to Bhūrbhuvaḥsvarloka.
