(8) You are the bearer; bear away the one who bears [us ill]. He who bears us ill, bear him away;

may we bear away him whom you bear. You are the best carrier of the gods, the most liberal, the most fulfilling, the most beloved, the most divine. You are the stride of Viṣṇu; you are the unoffered oblation, the gift of the sacrificial offering.

Be firm with your own call! I gaze upon you with the eye of Mitra for the sake of wide space and wind. Let the Vasus fumigate you with the Gāyatrī metre, like Aṅgiras; let the Rudras fumigate you with the Triṣṭubh metre;
let the Ādityas fumigate you with the Jagatī metre; let all the gods belonging to Vaiśvānara fumigate you.
With the Anuṣṭubh meter: May Indra fumigate you; may Varuṇa fumigate you; may Viṣṇu fumigate you;
[may the Ṛtus fumigate you]—to these and others, I offer incense; obeisance. "The Brāhmaṇa is his...
You are splendor, you are semen, you are light, you are the abode; you are the beloved of the gods, the inviolable place of sacrifice for the gods.

I take you for the deities, I take you for the deities; I take you for the gods, I take you for the sacrifices. To the Seasons (Ṛtus), etc., I offer this jewel-lamp; obeisance. To the Divine One (Devasya tvā), victory to Nārāyaṇa!
Having recited the playful hymn of praise to Śiva and Pārvatī, and having offered the chowrie to the Seasons, obeisance.
From joint to joint, may the parasol protect; that eye, may the mirror protect. To these deities, homage to the incense, homage to the lamp. To these [deities], homage to the garment.
May the entire ritual procedure of worship for these deities, beginning with the offering of the *arghya*, be completely fulfilled.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose from the mind of the Moon; once born, he was the sole Lord of all that exists.
He supported this earth and this heaven. To which God shall we offer worship with our oblation?
O Ṛtu, Viṣṇu, Pañcāyatana, and Devas, I present the honey-mixture (madhuparka), the sacrificial porridge (caru), and the measure (mātrā). Salutations to the Navel.
[He] offered a handful of flowers (*kusumāñjali*). There were seven prostrations (*praṇāma*) with the mantra "Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya;

O Blessed One, be gracious," and four circumambulations (*pradakṣiṇā*). [The Lord is] ever to be meditated upon as the destroyer of humiliation, the granter of desired objects, the abode of sacred pilgrimage sites, praised by Śiva and Brahmā, and the worthy refuge.

I revere your lotus-feet, O Great Being, which destroy the suffering of your dependents, protect those who bow before you, and serve as a boat across the ocean of existence— those feet by which you, the most righteous one, having abandoned the royal splendor so difficult to relinquish and coveted even by the gods,
went to the forest at the word of your noble father, and pursued the illusory deer desired by your beloved wife. I revere them.

I bow to that which is marked with a glorious lotus, barley-corn, goad, discus, bow, and fish; which has the hue of fresh, deep-red sprouts; which is the abode of Lakṣmī; the supreme auspiciousness; and the very form of the Self.
(2-3) Having wandered through all the cattle-pens of Gokula, he entered the interior of Vṛndāvana together with all the animals.
Desiring his own increase, he should contemplate that which belongs to the trees, beasts, and birds of the forest. (9)

I bow to that [garland] which, smeared with the saffron-paste from His breasts during the Rāsa dance, removed the fever of those gopīs whose bodies were enveloped by the fire born of separation, as they embraced Him upon their burning bosoms. (5)

I bow to Him whose form is beyond all desire, who was praised from afar by His wives— whose faces were distressed with grief at His departure— as He skillfully struck the head of Kālīya; (6) to Him, the abode of knowledge,
sought by the Vedas, beginningless, worthy of worship, and meditated upon in the heart by Brahmā and others of unfathomable wisdom.

I bow to [the Lord] who is the support for crossing over those fallen into the well of *saṃsāra*. (7) I bow to [the Lord] in the form of a cowherd; by Your foot, the mind of the one whose body was that of Aṅkapāla—intent on drinking from his breast—was captivated, so that the wheel turned in reverse, the vessel was shattered, and he fell to the ground. (8) Whoever recites this octet...

By quickly placing [the name] of the Supreme Person Nārāyaṇa, who delivers one from the ocean of hell, within their hearts, men attain all perfections and, upon the dissolution of the body, obtain liberation. With both knees, with my hands, my head, my chest, my mind, and my speech, I offer salutation.
Salutation! Food, salutation; clarified butter, salutation. On this day, may there be success today according to my resolve.

Whatever has occurred that was deficient in food, deficient in ritual action, deficient in procedure, deficient in materials, or deficient in mantra—may all that be without flaw and complete. May it be so. *Śanno devī*. To the Lord of the Seasons.

From these [verses] and others: *apośānaṃ namaḥ*, *ācamanīyaṃ namaḥ*. Again, [reciting] *śanno devī* and *ṛc*, I give a gift (*dakṣiṇā*) consisting of sesame, gold, silver, and a coin (*niṣka*). May these deities, together with the sacrificial fee, be pleased by the food; may they be satisfied. Having rendered [the offering] nectar-like (*amṛtīkṛtya*) by means of the Amṛteśa-mudrā, and so forth—all [is performed].

The Procedure for the Offering of Food (Naivedya): One should cast two flowers with the mantra *tad viṣṇoḥ*. Then, having performed the recitation (*japa*) and other rites, one should say: *oṃ bhūḥ puruṣaṃ visarjayāmi namaḥ*, *oṃ bhuvaḥ puruṣaṃ visarjayāmi*, *oṃ svaḥ puruṣaṃ visarjayāmi*, *oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ puruṣaṃ visarjayāmi*, *oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svastatsavitur*, and so forth—all [the mantras].

Having recited the Gāyatrī mantras, [I pray that] the worship of the fivefold abode of Viṣṇu (Viṣṇupañcāyatana-pūjana), performed for the sake of pleasing Śrī Viṣṇu, may be without flaw and complete—may it be so!
To these deities, obeisance with barley-water; obeisance with the water-libation (udakatarpaṇa)! O Lord, let your command be given to me.
"In the eating of this *naivedya*, O Lord, you ought to forgive me for the sake of accomplishing the maintenance of my body.
I am in distress; you are the refuge in all circumstances and at all times. O Lord, I have taken refuge in you;
protect me, who have come to you for shelter. Thus [is the recitation] of the hymns and so forth for the five deities.

Having recited: "I do not know invocation at all, I do not know worship at all; I do not know the portion of the offering—may it be forgiven, O Supreme Lord. With both knees [on the ground], etc., I perform prostration: *namaḥ*. "Salutation to Brahman" (*namo brahmaṇe*)—this is the libation (*tarpaṇa*). "With sacrifice, one should sacrifice the sacrifice" (*yajñena yajñaṃ yajeta*).

The dismissal (*visarjana*): "Bali, Vibhīṣaṇa, Bhīṣma, Prahlāda, Nārada, and Śuka—may these six, the foremost of Vaiṣṇavas, accept this water from the feet. *Oṃ namo devebhyaḥ*, etc. "O Blessed One, Lord of Kamalā, you have been worshipped by me with devotion; together with Lakṣmī, [enter] my heart."

"Enter for the sake of rest"—having thus petitioned, one should drink the nectar of the feet. The foot is pure, expansive, and ancient; by it, the son crosses over his evil deeds. Purified by that pure and holy [foot], may we cross over the great evil, the enemy. It is the radiant, luminous door of the world; the stream of the world.

O God of gods, Mahādeva, wielder of the conch, discus, and mace; O Viṣṇu, grant me permission to partake of the water from Your feet, which constantly bestows manifold milk upon the world of men. || 1 ||
Having drunk the water from the feet of Śrī Viṣṇu, which removes untimely death and wards off all diseases, there is no rebirth.
[Thus ends the ritual procedure for the worship of the fivefold abode of Viṣṇu.]
[Now, the procedure for the five products of the cow.]

Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and water infused with *kuśa* grass; this is designated as the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), which is purifying and cleanses the body. (1)
Having taken cow's urine with the Gāyatrī mantra, cow dung with "gandhadvārā," milk with "āpyāyasva," and curd with "dadhi krāvṇa."
"Tejo 'si" is prescribed for the ghee; "devasya tvā" for the kuśa-water;
cow's urine should be poured into the cow-dung, and likewise, [the other substances] should be mixed into the ghee. (3)
Having cast those [substances] into curd, all of that within the milk should be unified and placed in the midst of water infused with *kuśa* grass.
Having stirred it with the mantra "āpo hi ṣṭhā," one should drink it from a vessel made of udumbara wood, a lotus leaf, silver, or gold, while reciting the syllable Om.
One should drink that five-product mixture (pañcagavya), purified by mantras, three times;
with the mantra beginning "śuddhavati," one should scatter it in all directions.
One *pala* of the milk portion and an equal amount of cow urine are prescribed;
there should be one *pala* of ghee and two *tolakas* of cow dung.
The curd should be only a handful (prasṛta); this is remembered as the "five products of the cow" (pañcagavya).
Alternatively, equal portions of the five products of the cow are prescribed.
Having consecrated it with the root mantra, one should purify it with the tip of a blade of kusha grass;
by that, there shall be complete purification and the destruction of all sins.
The cow's urine should be from a copper-colored cow, the cow dung from a pure white cow,
the milk from a golden-colored cow, and likewise the curd from a blue-colored cow.
The ghee should be from a black cow, or else entirely from a Kapila cow;
there should be eight māṣas of cow urine and sixteen of cow dung.
Twelve parts of milk are prescribed, fifteen of curd are recorded,
and eighteen of clarified butter are declared as the proportions for the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
And nineteen māṣas of kuśa-water are prescribed;
one should place the cow-urine in the north and deposit the cow-dung in the west.

One should pour ghee in the south, curd in the east, milk in the center, and likewise kuśa-water in the northeast; this is the procedure for the preparation of the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
Varuṇa is the deity of urine; Havyavāhana (Agni) is that of cow dung;
Viṣṇu is that of milk; Soma is that of curd; and likewise, Pitṛmat is that of clarified butter. || 15 ||
In water with *kuśa* grass one becomes Brahmā; in the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), the deities themselves reside.
Even a killer of a mother, a killer of an embryo, or one who violates the teacher’s bed [is purified]. (16)
"Pañcagavya, when drunk even once, shall turn one away from sins."
Now, the mantras for casting [the arrow] in the various directions.
Let us praise this Indra; I, being pure, with a pure *sāman* chant, and with pure utterances, am purified by the rain and become possessed of blessings.
We shake [the Soma] for you, O Indra, who have grown strong like one liberated by the Aṅgirases;
desiring his many heroic deeds, we invoke him with offerings.
O Indra, you are pure; the impure have been struck down by you, who are pure with your pure aids.
Being pure, bestow wealth upon us; being pure and gracious, grant us prosperity.
For Indra, being pure, bestows wealth upon us; being pure, he grants treasures to the donor.
Being pure, you strike down the Vṛtras; being pure, we seek to win the prize of booty.
"Five dawns... [Thus ends the procedure for the five products of the cow.]
The Procedure for Eating.
[Now, the procedure for eating: First, having performed the smearing, it should be square for a Brāhmaṇa and triangular for a Kṣatriya.
The Vaiśya’s [purification] is said to be in the shape of a mandala, while that of the Śūdra is declared to be by sprinkling. || 1 ||
But those who eat their food with faces cast downwards without having prepared a mandala—
the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas consume the essence of that food.
One should eat while keeping five things moist, remaining silent, facing the east, and being pure;
these five—namely, the two hands, the two feet, and the mouth—are considered the "five moist" requirements.

Then, having brought the vessel of food, and having seen the food, one should first bow down and, with palms joined in reverence (*prāñjali*), say this: "May this be ours forever. Having thus recollected [this thought], one should offer salutation (*vandayet*). || 4 ||
Having taken the vessel of food with the Amṛta-mudrā:
"O Lord of Food, grant us food that is free from disease and full of vigor.
Further the giver; grant us strength for our two-footed and four-footed beings. (5)

Having consecrated it with the Gāyatrī mantra, he then sprinkles it with water: "Oṃ! That which is defiled by the remnants of food, that which is struck by sin, or [defiled] by death-impurity or birth-impurity—may the purifier of Vasu, Agni, and the rays of Savitṛ purify this food, as well as my evil deeds and whatever else [is impure]. Oṃ! That supreme [abode] of Viṣṇu... (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.2.13). Thus.

And then, on the ground in the southern part: "Oṃ, obeisance to the Lord of the Earth; Oṃ, obeisance to the Lord of the World; Oṃ, obeisance to the Lord of Beings. Having thus offered these three oblations (bali), [one says]: "Whosoever are stationed here or there, following the portion of the departed spirits (preta), may they all eat this smear-offering given by me right here upon this ground. Thus.

Having washed the smearings from the ground, [he recites]: "You move within all beings. Then, with the thought that the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, and it is poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman: "By him who is absorbed in the work of Brahman, Brahman alone is to be attained" (11). Having sipped water while reciting: "Oṃ, you are the support of immortality, svāhā."

With "Svāhā to Prāṇa," [one offers] with the index and middle fingers; with "Svāhā to Apāna," with the middle, ring, and thumb fingers; with "Svāhā to Samāna," with the little, ring, and thumb fingers; and with "Svāhā to Udāna," with the fingers excluding the index finger.
With the mantra "Svāhā to Vyāna," he should cause the oblation offered with all the fingers to enter through the tongue alone.

Having swallowed each morsel consecrated by the mantra of his chosen deity, and having purified his mouth with mouthfuls of water, he should sip water with the mantra: "Oṃ, you are the covering of nectar, svāhā."
"May those living beings who are full of longing, and those who are subject to the power of karma,
eat my leftovers— the remnants of the vessel that have been offered. Having consecrated [the food] with this mantra, one should pour the remaining food upon the ground.
With the thumb of the right hand [he touches] the big toe of the right foot:
"The Person the size of a thumb, who rests upon the tip of the thumb, the Lord of the entire world, the Master—may He, the consumer of all, be pleased. Having thus immersed [the foot], he says:

"May Śaryāti, Sukanyā, Śakra, Cyavana, and the two Aśvins—may these six always bestow upon me the Gāruḍī vision. Having thus touched water with his thumbs at his eyes while remembering his chosen deity, [he recites]: "Prāṇo 'gniḥ..."
The Supreme Self indeed rests upon the five vital airs; may He, the consumer of the universe, being pleased, please the entire world. 15.
You are the All; you are Vaiśvānara; being born, you illuminate the universe.
All oblations enter into you, as do all creatures—wherever you are, there you are the immortal one. 16.
Becoming Vaiśvānara and taking refuge in the bodies of living beings, joined with the prāṇa and apāna breaths, I digest the four kinds of food.
I am food, I am the giver of food, I am the eater of food.
One should always remember Agastya, Kumbhakarṇa, Bhīma, and the submarine fire (Vaḍavānala) at the end of a meal; then no disease will arise in the stomach.
May there be welfare for kings, and likewise may there be welfare for the twice-born, for cows, and for all subjects.
May the entire world be free from affliction, and may all defects come to destruction. Thus.
One should recite.
[Thus concludes the procedure for eating.]
[Now, the Praise of the Guru:

Oṃ! [I bow to the Guru who is] the bliss of Brahman, the bestower of supreme happiness, the embodiment of absolute knowledge, transcending all dualities, resembling the sky, and the reality indicated by such mantras as "That Thou Art."

I bow to that true Guru, who is one, eternal, stainless, and immovable; who has become the witness of all cognitions, who transcends all states of being, and who is devoid of the three qualities (guṇas). || 1 ||
Constantly recollecting the fear of birth and death, having developed a state of world-weariness, and meditating again and again upon Paśupati, the beloved of Umā, who dwells within;
drinking again and again the stream of the nectar of supreme bliss, [one attains liberation].
Again and again, I bow to the pair of lotus feet of my own guru. || 2 ||
For that high-souled one who has supreme devotion for the Divine, and for the Guru as for the Divine, these truths thus declared are indeed revealed. (3)
I bow my head with devotion to the true Guru, who is peaceful, manifest as the very form of Śiva, seated upon the seat of yoga, for the sake of attaining dharma, kāma, and artha. 4.
I bow to the glorious Guru, supreme bliss, whose very form is bliss;
by his mere presence, the highest consciousness-bliss arises.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
Salutations to that illustrious Guru, by whom the eye of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance has been opened with the ointment-stick of knowledge. (7)
When Hari is angry, the Guru is the protector; when the Guru is angry, there is no one at all. Salutations to that venerable Guru, who is the embodiment of all the gods. (8)
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, and the Guru is Maheśvara himself;
the Guru alone is the entire universe—salutations to that venerable Guru.
The root of meditation is the form of the Guru; the root of worship is the feet of the Guru;
the root of knowledge is the word of the Guru; the root of liberation is the grace of the Guru. (10)
Salutations to you, O Lord, Blessed One, Śiva in the form of the Guru, who has assumed manifold forms for the sake of perfectly accomplishing the descent of knowledge. 11.
Salutations to You, who are ever-new and of ever-new form, whose single nature is the ultimate reality,
the sun that shatters the darkness of all ignorance, and the mass of pure consciousness.
Salutations to the Supreme Self, who is independent yet assumes a form out of compassion;
who is dependent upon his devotees for their sake, and who is the cause of the welfare of those destined for liberation. || 13 ||
To the one who is the form of knowledge for the wise, the light for those who illuminate;
to the discernment for the discriminating, and the reflective awareness for those possessed of insight.
In front, at my sides, behind, above, and below,
may you always grant me your seat through the form of my own mind.
[Thus ends the Praise of the Holy Guru.
[Now begins the Praise of Mahāgāyatrī:
Constantly searching throughout the three worlds for the Mother of the Vedas,
Having today attained a state established by the conscious Self (cid-ātman),
I bow with tears and a faltering voice out of great joy, seeking by means of this boat of devotion to swiftly cross the ocean of calamities so difficult to traverse. || 1 ||
Indeed, the compassion of the virtuous, which falls upon those most wretched, shines forth most brilliantly; therefore, O Mother, with Your moon-like eye, look upon a person such as me!
For even though You are ever-new, O Sovereign, You do not diminish by protecting us.
For it is because of his existence that the state of being a bad son does not appear in the heart of the mother.
I bow to [the Lord] who is beautiful with half-glancing eyes that possess the luster of coral, molten gold, black, and pure white;
[eyes] which shine like the sun, the friend of the lotus-cluster, or like molten gold.
Adorned with the jewels of their crowns and embellished by fragments of the moon.
Her form shines with five faces,
possessing a splendor like the bow of the Lord of the Gods, and she is worshipped by all the deities;
she holds in her hands the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, the goad, the skull-bowl, the trident, and the conch.
She was resplendent with hands marked by the two qualities of the essence of beauty (kṛsārasa).
I bow to Śivā, who has become the root of the tree of worldly existence, who is worshipped by the lords of sages, who causes the manifestation of the entire circle of unbroken reality,
who embodies all the deities, and who bestows all supernatural accomplishments.
[She beheld] Sarasvatī, who removes the suffering of worldly existence, possessing a form and body that were unprecedented.
She whose eyes are the pure moon and sun, whose form is the pure moon and sun,
who possesses a nature characterized by the union of the pure moon and sun, the auspicious one;
she who is served by the circle of her own powers, out of compassion for her two feet.
I worship the supreme power of the Supreme Lord, who is the most beautiful in the three worlds.
She who is the personified sovereignty of the Great Lord Maheśvara— over the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the world—
became a creeper-like form with a body that manifests through various divisions such as the two-fold and three-fold.
May she, the sovereign of the three Vedas, always arise for the conquest of the world. || 7 ||
I bow to those five lotus-faces, which remove all impurity, whose single stalk is the throat, which are ever-blossoming, born of devotion,
served by the swans of my own devotees, and which are the kinsmen of the pure moon and the lotus.
For their bodies, which served as the means of perception, have indeed returned to the five elements.
With a mind desiring to support those people whose hearts are scorched by the unbearable heat of the afflictions (*ādhi*) in the ocean of existence, and who are constantly tormented by the six waves;
[she is] always [attended] by Brahmins whose lotus-faces are radiant with the resonance of the Vedas.
May that Sovereign Goddess, praised at the three junctions of the day, indeed grant us happiness. || 9 ||

The daughter of the three [gods], whose impurities of devotion were shaken away by the fall of her own glance, is joyfully praised by impartial people according to the distinctions of their respective caste-duties;
she [is like] the celestial river in the guise of water produced from washing her feet.
If she has come to this earth, may she grant us auspiciousness. || 10 ||
O Goddess, if you suspect everyone as being deceived by their own hypocrisy, their minds addicted to base enjoyments, ever impure, treading the wrong path, and deceitful—
how then can there be the majesty arising from the contemplation of your own feet?
For you look with eyes of compassion upon one who contemplates your feet, but not upon one such as I.
Though she is free from discrimination regarding those corrupted by manifold defects, she is the independent power, the Sovereign who destroys the sins of worldly existence;
casting her compassionate gaze upon one who has become a vessel for her devotion—
May he, like a honey-bee, rest upon my lotus-like face day and night. || 12 ||
Recalling at the three junctions of the day his chosen deity and the hymn born from the mouth of the beautiful Keśava, with a heart kindled by devotion and having performed the Mother of the Vedas,
he shall shake off the accumulation of sins and bestow supreme fame.
Having slain [the enemy] there, he attains the state of absolute liberation, free from fear. || 13 ||
[Thus ends the "Praise of the Playful Līlā of the Great Gāyatrī.
[The Praise of Petition.]

Oṃ! Frightened by the darkness of existence which is so difficult to overcome, I bow to the deity beginning with Brahmā, who alone possesses the eye that destroys it, for the sake of annihilating delusion. 1.
O Goddess, remove for me the miserable rebirths accumulated over hundreds of lifetimes; having reached the shade of the wish-fulfilling tree, how could people suffer? (2)
"O Gāyatrī, look at me with your affectionate eyes; I am terrified.
Ambikā does not leave behind her young, weak son when he is at the forefront. (3)
Come, quickly grant me this auspicious boon with your lotus-like hand;
come to me, who am distressed by great delusion and miserable, and touch me constantly.
O Mother, one who is afflicted does not wait; therefore, be gracious to me quickly.
O Sāvitrī, setting aside your rosary, look upon me here without hindrance.
For one who listens, there may be no other duty; therefore, perform that which is for the welfare of others.
O Sovereign of the Gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, and the others take refuge in you. (6) Thus ends the prayer and praise.
[Now follows the praise of Sarasvatī.]

Oṃ! O you of white complexion, O ornament, O Sarasvatī, O support of all speech, O bestower of boons upon the mind of the Lotus-born [Brahmā], O you who are as bright as the moon—salutations to you! || 1 ||
Blessed indeed is he in this world, he alone is worthy of worship, he alone is the teacher of all, in whose lotus-bud of a mouth you, O Kuladevatā consisting of speech, reside. (2)
Who else but you is the possessor of discernment? For one devoid of discernment, life is fruitless.
Therefore, O Bhāratī, you alone are the cause of discernment for living beings.
Even a man who is prosperous, heroic, fortunate, and endowed with beauty and grace, when deprived of you, appears like a bull in the assembly of the gods—though he be otherwise pure. (4)
O Mother! Even a dull-witted man becomes honored by sages and men, becomes skillful, and becomes an expounder of all the scriptures through meditation upon your mantra. || 5 ||

Where indeed in their homes do those women with eyes like blue lotuses, bent low by the weight of their breasts, sport, as long as you, O Goddess with eyes like dark lotuses, are not satisfied with living beings on earth? (6)
Whatever a man attains after conquering an enemy king—accompanied by elephants, camels, oxen, horses, men, and wealth—all that is the fruit of his praise of your feet. (7)
Even when won over with great difficulty in this life, Fortune abandons a man;
yet, thinking "you do not [leave] those who possess true masters," who would not praise you?
O Goddess Pañcamukhīśvarī, O Vāgīśvarī, you who move with the confidence of a bee wandering within the lotus-like faces of the best of poets—salutations be unto you! || 9 ||
That person who praises with devotion the speech prostrated before Śambhu shall, in no time at all, become a king among poets, with the flow of his intellect fully attentive. 10.
[Thus ends the hymn to Sarasvatī composed by Kālidāsa.
[Now follows the hymn to Gaurī.]

Oṃ! I praise Ambā Gaurī, whose lotus-like eyes possess a mass of radiance equal to a row of rising suns; she who has established and yet dissolved all worlds through her divine play, and who is sought within the heart by yogins who have transcended the world.
I bow to that slender-waisted Goddess, who brings about the destruction of the afflictions of the bonds of desire for those men intent on meditating upon her lotus feet,
and who occupies half the body of Lord Śiva.
Gaurī, my Mother, whose eyes are like lotuses. || 2 ||

To her who consists of truth, knowledge, and bliss, who flashes like lightning, and who eternally brings about the pinnacle of liberation within the minds of those established in withdrawal, meditation, and samādhi;
Gaurī, the Mother, whose eyes are like lotuses. || 3 ||
I bow to the lotus-eyed Gaurī, whose face is graced by a gentle smile that delights Candrāpīḍa, whose mass of shimmering curls is adorned by Candrāpīḍa,
and whose pair of lotus-feet are worshipped by Indra, Upendra, and the other gods.
She who, though herself one, sports at her own will pervading the worlds with various forms and multitudes of powers—
that auspicious Gaurī, the Mother, the lotus-eyed one, who is like a wish-fulfilling creeper for those who bow before her. 5.
Having risen from the *mūlādhāra*, having passed through the aperture of Brahmā and abandoned the solar and lunar abodes,
her limbs ablaze— her who is gross,
subtle, and most subtle, and worthy of worship— I bow to her.
I bow to the lotus-eyed Mother Gaurī.
I bow to that Mother Gaurī, whose lotus-eyes are beautiful, who shines in the form of the syllables from 'a' to 'kṣa', who gives birth to the multitude of beings in every single being,
and who consists of the bliss of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman).
In whose two armpits the entire universe-egg is concealed, yet emerges again and again in its very unimpaired state—
[I bow] to that lotus-eyed Mother Gaurī, who sports with her Lord upon the crystal mountain.
In whom all this—both the moving and the unmoving—is woven together, like a string of gems upon a thread;
that lotus-eyed Mother Gaurī, who is to be reached by the path of spiritual knowledge (adhyātma-jñāna), [I salute]. 9.

I bow to Ambā, the lotus-eyed Gaurī, wife of Śiva, whose nature is to sport in the protection of the universe; she who is eternal, true, partless, the one Lord of the world, and the witness of its creation and dissolution.
To him who, at dawn, constantly recites the *Gaurī-daśaka* with devotion while cultivating purity of heart,
the Daughter of the Mountain will surely grant perfection of speech, abundant prosperity, and devotion to Śiva.
He ordains. || 11 ||
[Thus ends the Śrīgaurīstuti.]
[Now begins the hymn of praise, the Mukunda-mālā.]
Oṃ, I bow to Mukunda, whose eyes are as long as the petals of a lotus, whose teeth are like jasmine, the moon, and a conch shell, who wears the attire of a young cowherd,
whose footstool is worshipped by hosts of gods led by Indra, whose abode is Vṛndāvana, and who is the son of Vasudeva.

O Mukunda, make me speak every day thus: "O Śrīvallabha, O Varada, O you who are devoted to compassion, O beloved of your devotees, O you who are skilled in plundering worldly existence, O Nātha, O you who recline upon the serpent, O Abode of the Universe!"

Victory, victory to this Lord, the delight of Devakī! Victory, victory to Kṛṣṇa, the lamp of the Vṛṣṇi clan! Victory, victory to the one dark as a rain-cloud, whose limbs are tender! Victory, victory to Mukunda, the destroyer of the earth’s burden! || 3 ||
Having prostrated with my head at the feet of Mukunda, I beseech you for this one exclusive request:
by your grace, may there be no forgetting of your lotus-feet in birth after birth. || 4 ||
The honey from the lotus feet of the glorious Mukunda is supremely wonderful;
those who drink it are not deluded, while those who do not drink it are deluded.
I do not worship the pair of your feet for the sake of attaining freedom from dualities;
nor, O Hari, to remove even the heavy hellish torment of Kumbhīpāka;
nor even to sport in the Nandana grove with lovely gardens and tender-bodied creepers.
In every state of being, within the temple of my heart, may I meditate upon you.
I have no attachment to dharma, nor to the accumulation of wealth, nor indeed to the enjoyment of sensual pleasures;
whatever may be my destiny, O Blessed One, let it be in accordance with my past karma.
This alone is what I desire and hold most dear, even in birth after birth.
May there be unwavering devotion directed toward the pair of your lotus feet. || 7 ||
O Destroyer of Hell, let my dwelling be wherever I desire—in heaven, on earth, or even in hell;
yet at the moment of death, I shall contemplate only Your feet, which bear the blossoming autumnal lotuses of Śāradā.
O mind, do not cease from sporting here with the lotus-eyed Murāri, who holds the conch and discus;
I know of no other pleasure that is ever equal to the nectar of remembering the feet of Hari. 9.
Do not fear, O dull-witted one! Reflecting thus in many ways for a long time, realize that these torments cannot prevail over us; for our Lord is indeed Śrīdhara.
Casting aside indolence, meditate upon Nārāyaṇa, who is easily attained through devotion.
If he is capable of removing the calamities of the world, is he not capable of [removing] those of a servant? || 10 ||
"Do not let your heart fall into despondency, thinking, 'How shall I cross this unfathomable and difficult-to-traverse ocean of existence?
For your singular devotion, fixed upon the lotus-eyed Lord who destroys the hellish realms, will certainly carry you across."

O You who possess the three bodies, for us who are sinking in the great ocean called saṃsāra— an ocean whose water is craving, which is tossed by the winds of passion, garlanded with waves of delusion, possessing whirlpools of wives, and crowded with swarms of crocodiles that are one's own children— [grant protection].
O Giver of Boons! Be gracious toward the boat of devotion for your lotus feet. || 12 ||
The earth is but a particle of dust, the waters are mere droplets, fire is a feeble spark, the wind is a faint breath, space is a most subtle aperture, and all the gods,
from Rudra and Pitāmaha down to the rest, are but insignificant insects.
Wherein that which is seen by you triumphs, O Bhūman, until the limit of the liberated (avadhūta). 13.
The study of the Vedas is like weeping in a wilderness; daily observances of arduous vows yield only the fruit of division; rites of public charity are all like offerings poured into ashes;
and even the bathing in sacred fords is like an elephant’s bath—unless it be at his feet.
Victorious is that Lord Nārāyaṇa, whose praise is like a lotus amidst the pairs of opposites. || 14 ||
For those caught in the ocean of existence, struck by the winds of dualities, burdened with the weight of protecting sons, daughters, and wives,
and sinking without a raft in the turbulent waters of the sense-objects, Viṣṇu alone is the boat that serves as a refuge.
Of men. || 15 ||
For those fallen into the dust of passion, shrouded by the net of delusion, and beset by the miserable state of birth and death;
for the helpless who have no refuge, he alone is the protector and the one who leads the afflicted onto the path of virtue.
Cakrapāṇi [is the lord] of men. || 16 ||
O Hari! I am fallen into the depths of the terrible ocean of worldly existence, crowded with thousands of offenses;
I have no other resort and have come to you for refuge—out of mere compassion, make me your own. 17.
Whatever has been thought by the mind, whatever has been spoken by the voice, and whatever movement of the eyes, hands, ears, or feet has been performed;
whatever has been done by me alone during nights and days—let all that become an act of worship unto You, O Janārdana!
May I have no womanhood, may I have no state of servitude, may I have no foolishness, and may I not be born in wretched lands.
May I never have false views; in birth after birth, may I remain a devotee of Viṣṇu. || 19 ||
"Ānanda! Govinda! Mukunda! Rāma! Nārāyaṇa! Ananta! Nirāmaya!"—though capable of uttering these names, no one speaks them; alas, such is the worldly affliction of people regarding liberation! 20.
Salutations to Mādhava, the enemy of Madhu, whose beautiful form is starred by the spray from the waves of the milk-ocean, and who reclines upon the couch of the serpent’s coils.
O Son of Nanda, if you have fled out of fear, having abandoned the essence of the milk-ocean, why do you not dissolve yourself within my mind, which is utterly shrouded in darkness? 22.
Because He bestows fearlessness out of parental affection, because He extinguishes the suffering of the distressed,
because He is magnanimous, because He dries up sins, and because He grants the state of unsurpassed bliss beyond counting—
the Lord of Śrī alone is to be served by all the worlds; this is the witness of those who see clearly.
Prahlāda, Vibhīṣaṇa, Karirāṭ, Pāñcālya, Ahalyā, and Dhruva. || 23 ||
While the Lord Śrī Puruṣottama— the sole sovereign of the three worlds, who is to be served with the mind, the giver of his own station, and the supreme Nārāyaṇa— remains present,
[people worship] some base man, a mere lord of a few villages who bestows only meager wealth.
"Alas, we fools and wretches search for a man for the sake of service! (24)
O people, listen! Those sages skilled in yoga, such as Yājñavalkya and others, proclaim this remedy for birth, death, and disease:
let the internal light—the immeasurable, singular, immortal one known as Kṛṣṇa—be drunk in.
When that supreme medicine is drunk, it brings about ultimate nirvāṇa. || 25 ||
With palms joined in reverence, head bowed low, limbs bristling with horripilation,
voice choked with emotion, and eyes shedding streams of tears—
constantly tasting the nectar of meditating upon the pair of your lotus feet.
O lotus-eyed one, may our life always be fruitful! || 26 ||

O tongue, as you utter words that speak the supreme truth beyond all else, they seem to pour forth nectar; therefore, with palms joined in reverence, cause me to repeat the names that have Nārāyaṇa as their object.
This body, fragile due to its inevitable transformation and shattered by the joints of old age, will surely fall;
why do you weary yourself with medicines, O fool of wicked mind? Drink the medicine of Kṛṣṇa, which is free from all ailment. 28.
Having uttered the glorious name known as Nārāyaṇa, what even among the sinful has not obtained their desire?
Alas! Our speech did not previously proceed toward it; therefore, we have experienced the suffering of dwelling in the womb and so forth.
May I never behold those whose merit is exhausted, who for even a moment lack devotion to Your lotus feet;
may I never hear Your narrated deeds, which are so worthy of being heard, having abandoned all other tales;
and may I never, O Mādhava, fail to touch with my heart even You, the Lord of the universe, while denying Him.
May I never be deprived of the practice of serving you, even in birth after birth. || 30 ||
O Madana, abandon your presence within my mind, which is the abode of the lotus feet of Mukunda!
You have been emaciated by the fire of Śiva’s eye; do you not remember the prowess of Murāri’s discus? 31.
The ocean is your wife; this Viriñci is your son;
the Vedas are your hymn of praise; the host of gods is your retinue of servants;
liberation is your grace; and this entire world is situated within you, O Goddess Devakī.
My mother, my friend, the enemy of my strength, and my son—in truth, I know nothing else.
O tongue, proclaim Keśava, the enemy of Mura; O mind, worship Śrīdhara; O pair of hands, honor the stories of Acyuta; O pair of ears, you must listen!
O pair of eyes, behold Kṛṣṇa; O feet, go to the abode of Hari’s two feet!
Smell the *tulasī* from Mukunda’s feet with your nose; bow your head to Adhokṣaja. || 33 ||
That head alone is auspicious which is whitened by the dust from prostrating before Kṛṣṇa;
those eyes alone are beautiful which are freed from darkness and by which Hari is seen; that intellect alone is pure through its observances and restraints which meditates upon Mādhava.
That tongue is a showerer of nectar which, at every step, praises Nārāyaṇa. || 34 ||
He is the emerald for the serpents of hatred toward His devotees, the jewel that protects the three worlds, the gem-like cloud for the *cātaka* birds of the Gopīs' eyes, and the seal-ring of beauty.
He is the crest-jewel of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds, the sole ornament upon the pair of full breasts of Rukmiṇī.
May the crest-jewel of those to be meditated upon for the highest good, the crown-jewel of the cowherds, grant us [blessings]. || 35 ||

The sole mantra for the destruction of enemies, the mantra most honored by all the words of the Upaniṣads, the mantra that delivers one from saṃsāra, the mantra for the departure from the company of those shrouded in accumulated darkness,
the sole mantra for all sovereignty, and the mantra for protection against being bitten by the serpent of calamity.
O tongue, constantly recite, recite the mantra of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the mantra that brings fulfillment to one’s birth. 36.

The medicine that eradicates delusion, the medicine for the functioning of the mind and mental states of the Sage, the medicine that destroys the calamities of the Daityas, the sole life-restoring medicine for the three worlds,
the medicine that pacifies the suffering of devotees, the medicine that utterly destroys the fear of worldly existence— this is the divine medicine.
O mind, drink the medicine of the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, which brings about the attainment of the highest good! (37)
This is indeed a marvel in the world of men: they abandon the nectar and drink poison;
casting aside the names pertaining to Nārāyaṇa, these deceivers recite other words. (38)
The eyes of the women of Lāṭa, their pitcher-like breasts, their playful chambers, and the slopes of their arms—foolish poets spend their days describing such things as "sandalwood trees.
But [the wise] call out, "Govinda! Janārdana! Lord of the worlds! Kṛṣṇa!"
Through such expressions, the convention passes among those men whose minds are focused solely upon that [object]. || 39 ||

There exists for me a provision for the journey on this great departure—the fortunate lot of the nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s name—which cannot be begged for, cannot be bought, is never stale, does not require cooking, is inexhaustible, and is easy to carry. 40.

This hymn was composed by King Kulaśekhara— a bee at the lotus-feet of the Lotus-eyed Lord— for those kings whose two beloved friends, Śruta-dhara and Ravi-loka-gīta, were like auspicious attendants to his twice-born family. [The *Mukunda-mālā* hymn composed by the illustrious King Kulaśekhara.]
[Now, the divine pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa]
Oṃ! Having sought the Supreme Brahman branch by branch throughout the tree of the Vedas, I have now found it in the embrace of the lotus-eyed damsels of Gokula. || 1 ||
The penance performed by others has borne fruit for these cowherd girls,
since the Supreme Brahman dwells within their jar-like breasts like a dark blue veil.
Let others devote themselves to the Śruti, others to the Smṛti, and others to the Mahābhārata, being afraid of worldly existence;
I too bow to Nanda, in whose courtyard dwells the Supreme Brahman.
What shall we say, to whom, or whose mind will find conviction?
The Supreme Brahman delights in the bower-cottages of the cowherd girls.
I bow to the Cowherd Child who, crying out, "The fresh butter has been taken away! By whom was my milk drunk? Where is my flute? rolls upon the ground.
Behold the power of these women; for in their unclouded hearts they have bound that formless Supreme Brahman, drawn by the rays of their slender glances.
O mind, you who are distressed by anxiety! I constantly entreat you: do not worry over these flickering objects of sense, such as home, wife, and the like.
[Seek instead] Him who is dark as a blue cloud, singing at the foot of a tree on the banks of the Yamunā.
Meditate upon Gopāla, who wears a forest garland, who is lotus-like, the son of Nanda. || 7 ||
If yogis, through a mind mastered by the practice of meditation, perceive that supreme light which is devoid of qualities and free from action, let them see it;
but for us, may that very same light long continue to be a marvel for our eyes.
On the banks of the Kālindī, that indescribable blue darkness runs away. (Thus ends the *Kṛṣṇalīlā*).
Now follows the *Jayastuti* of Viṣṇu.
Oṃ! Victory, O Nārāyaṇa! Victory, O Puruṣottama! Victory, O Vāmana! O enemy of Kaṃsa!
Lift me up, O destroyer of the lords of the Asuras! I have fallen into this cycle of existence;
O Keśava, enemy of hell, remove my terrible burden of sin!
Out of compassion for me, who am wretched and helpless, lead me to the further shore of the ocean of existence. || 1 ||
Victory, victory to you, O God! Victory, O Destroyer of Asuras! Victory, O Keśava! Victory, O Viṣṇu!
Victory, O Bee at the lotus-face of Lakṣmī! Victory, O Conqueror of the Ten-headed One! (The Ghora [Section], 2).
You are the mother, the father, and the Lord, O Acyuta; you are the son, the friend, and the wealth;
you are the refuge for those who have come for shelter, O you who are compassionate toward those seeking protection; you are the vessel for crossing the terrible ocean of worldly existence. 3.
Again birth, again death, and again dwelling in the womb—I am able to endure this, O Mādhava! Lift up me, your own servant. (The Chorus) 4.

O Kṛṣṇa, O Supreme Person! Hold in your mind that which was sung by the eminent sage Śaṅkara, who is devoted to the feet of the husband of Janaka’s daughter; ward off the fear of the terrible cycle of worldly existence. 5.

O Hari! Although I perceive that there is not even the slightest thing possessing substantial reality within this entire universe, nevertheless, O Acyuta, this infatuation with sons and wife does not leave me. (6) [Thus ends the praise of Viṣṇu.
[The Govindāṣṭaka]
Oṃ! Truth, knowledge, infinite, eternal, formless, the supreme ether; playful in wandering through cow-pens and courtyards; effortless, yet the supreme effort;
possessing various forms fashioned by *māyā*, yet formless, yet having the form of the universe.
Bow down to Govinda, the lord of the earth, who is himself without a protector, the supreme bliss. || 1 ||
"I am eating clay!"—with these words, Yaśodā struck him;

yet he, who had looked upon the world with a wide-open mouth during his childhood terror, beheld the fourteen worlds including the Lokāloka mountain, the primary pillar for the cities of the three worlds, the light of the world that is beyond darkness, the Lord of the World, the Supreme Lord. (2)
The destroyer of the enemies of the gods of the triple heaven, the remover of the earth’s burden, the healer of the disease of worldly existence;
absolute liberation, the food of fresh butter, yet without food, the sustenance of the universe;
the manifestation of the particular state of the mind’s activity made clear through purity, yet without manifestation—the Śaiva state, absolute and tranquil.
I bow to Gopāla, whose form is the play of the Lord; to Gopāla, the protector of the lineage; to Gopāla, who is cherished by the sport of the gopīs and the play of upholding Govardhana;
to him whose name Govinda is clearly proclaimed by the cows, yet who possesses many names; and who is far beyond the range of the senses of even the gods.
The breaking of the circle of the cowherd girls’ assembly, appearing as a state of separation yet devoid of actual division;
possessing the good fortune of being greyed by the dust raised and scattered by the hooves of the moon-white cows;
an inconceivable bliss grasped through faith and devotion, whose true nature is ever-meditated upon.
The wish-fulfilling gem and the power of atomization. || 5 ||
Then, as she was about to take the garments of the women who were busy bathing,
they, now clad only in the directions of space, drew near to give her clothes; yet he,
having shaken off the delusion of the two-fold sorrow, was the Buddha dwelling within the intellect, whose body is pure existence alone.
I bow to the Beloved, the cause of causes, the primordial and beginningless one, who appears like a dense mass of time;

who dances repeatedly upon the head of the serpent Kāliya in the Yamunā; who is Time itself, yet transcends the divisions of time; who has encompassed all things, knows the defects of the Kali age, and is the cause of the movement through the three periods of time.
In the land of Vṛndāvana, may I behold the host of gods, and here, the one worshipped by the multitude (Vṛndā), who is worthy of praise;
whose gentle smile is as pure as a jasmine flower; who is the bliss of his own self and the joy of his friends;
and whose pair of feet, which are the source of bliss, are worshiped in their minds by all venerable great sages.
I bow to the one who is an ocean of all virtues. || 8 ||
He who, with his mind dedicated to Govinda, recites this *Govindāṣṭaka*:
"O Govinda! O Acyuta! O Mādhava! O Viṣṇu! O Leader of Gokula!
O Kṛṣṇa!"—he has all his sins washed away by the water of meditation upon the lotus-feet of Govinda.
One attains Govinda, who dwells within as the nectar of supreme bliss.
[Thus ends the *Govindāṣṭaka* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
[Now begins the *Śivastuti*.]

Oṃ! With my mind absorbed in You, I worship in my heart Bhairavanātha—the refuge of the helpless—who pervades all specific beings, both moving and unmoving; who is composed of consciousness, one, infinite, and beginningless. 1.
Through the power of your grace, this entire world now appears to me as consisting of you alone;
and since you, O Great Lord, are forever my very self, therefore everything is composed of my own self.
Since You, the Lord who pervades the universe, are one’s own self, there can be no talk of fear of worldly existence;
even though the multitudes of karmas exist that produce unbearable suffering, delusion, and terror. (3)
O Antaka! Do not direct this gaze of yours, so exceedingly fierce with wrath, toward me;
for I am steadfast through meditation on the service of Śaṅkara and am composed of the terrifying power of Bhairava. (4)

O Lord, since the dense darkness [of ignorance] has been rent asunder by the rays of consciousness consisting of You who have thus arisen, I am never afraid of the ghouls of death, Yama, Antaka, and karma; homage be to You! 5.

O You, whose rays awaken the truth that has emerged and who have sprinkled the true nature of all worldly objects with them—I find my rest in You, the Self, who are completely filled with the supreme nectar of existence. 6.

O Lord! Just as soon as the state of affliction, which inflicts intense torment, comes within the range of my mind, at that very moment there arises a shower of nectar consisting of hymns of praise for the non-duality of "I" and "mine."
O Śaṅkara! This is true: vows, charity, ritual bathing, and austerity destroy the heat of worldly existence;
yet, when the mind is saturated with the nectar-like contemplation of your scriptures, it flows with streams of bliss.

O Lord Bhairava, this consciousness of mine dances, sings, and rejoices intensely, having attained you—the beloved, the uniquely beautiful one, difficult for other people to find, and the knower of the sacred pledge (samaya). || 9 ||

In the month of Pauṣa, on the tenth day of the dark fortnight, Abhinavagupta composed this hymn, by which the compassionate Lord instantly allays the torment of the desert of worldly existence for his people. 10.
[Thus ends the *Śivastuti* composed by the teacher Abhinavagupta.]
